Start here

Welcome to The Well Listed Kit.

This kit helps UK sellers write clear, accurate listings, price items from real sold listings, and reply to buyers politely, using the free AI chat tools you probably already have on your phone.

It is not software and there is nothing to install. It is a set of tested prompts (instructions you copy and paste into an AI tool), fill-in templates and checklists. You bring the item and the facts. The prompts make the AI do the tidy, time-consuming writing, in UK English, without inventing anything.

We cannot promise you more sales, and nobody honestly can. What the kit does is help you write listings faster that are clear, complete and honest, which is exactly what buyers look for.

Your first listing in 5 minutes

Pick one item you want to sell today. Something simple, like a jumper or a book.

Minute 1: fill in a brief. Open Module 01, copy the brief for your category and fill in what you know. Measure it if it is clothing. Write flaws plainly: where, what, how big. Leave blanks if you do not know.

Minute 2: open your AI tool. Start a new chat in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Copilot (free versions are fine).

Minute 3: paste the starter prompt below with your brief.

Minute 4: fix the [CHECK] notes. The AI will mark anything missing with [CHECK: ...]. Find the fact (look at the label, measure, test it) or delete the line.

Minute 5: read it next to the item and post. Does every word match the item and the photos? If yes, copy it into the listing form.

The 5-minute starter prompt

You are helping a UK seller write one listing for [PLATFORM]. Using ONLY the facts in my Listing Brief below, write:

1. A title that fits [PLATFORM]'s current title limit (eBay UK: 80 characters; if unsure, keep it under 60) with the character count.
2. A short description: what it is, measurements or dimensions, condition with every flaw (where, what, how big), what is included, postage.
3. The values for the main fields the platform asks for (brand, size, colour, condition, material).

Rules:
- UK English (colour, jumper, trousers, postage, trainers).
- Use only facts in my brief. If something important is missing, write [CHECK: what is missing]. Never invent measurements, materials, dates or test results.
- Keep every flaw. Do not soften any.
- No hype words (stunning, amazing, must have), no exclamation marks, no emoji.
- No misleading claims: do not say rare, vintage, genuine, new or fully working unless my brief says so.
- No other brand names.
- Do not reveal my lowest price.

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

When you have done one, move on to the platform-specific prompts in Modules 02 to 04. They go further than the starter prompt.

Choosing a free AI tool

Every prompt in this kit works in the free versions of the main AI chat tools. No plugins, no paid features, no internet browsing needed.

ToolWhere to get itGood to know
ChatGPTApp or websiteWidely used. Free version has usage limits
ClaudeApp or websiteGood at following detailed rules. Free version has usage limits
GeminiApp or website, and built into many Android phonesHandy if you already use Google apps
CopilotApp or website, and built into Windows and EdgeHandy if you use a Windows laptop

Free versions and their limits change often, so do not worry too much about which one. Pick the one you already have, or try two and keep the one whose writing you prefer.

Tips that apply to all of them:

  • One chat per item, or per batch. Starting a new chat stops details from one item leaking into another.
  • Paste the whole prompt. The rules at the bottom are what keep the AI honest and in UK English.
  • If the answer is wrong, say so. "The size is 14, not 12. Rewrite using only the brief." works well.
  • AI tools miscount characters. Always check the title length in the listing form itself.
  • You are the editor. The AI drafts. You check every fact before you post.

What about the AI tools built into the platforms? Some marketplaces now have their own AI listing helpers (eBay's app can draft a listing from a photo, Depop can generate a description from a photo, and Amazon offers generative listing tools to UK sellers). They can be useful. The same rule applies: check every word against the item. You can also paste their draft into our prompts (for example D10 in Module 03) to tidy it into UK English and remove anything unsupported.

Privacy: what never goes into an AI tool

AI chat tools are not the place for other people's personal data. Treat them like a public notice board.

Never paste:

  • Buyers' names, addresses, phone numbers or email addresses
  • Order numbers, tracking numbers linked to a person, or screenshots of order pages
  • A buyer's messages with their username showing (replace it with [BUYER])
  • Your own bank details, passwords, account login codes or home address

Safe to paste:

  • Facts about the item (your Listing Brief)
  • Sold listing titles and prices you have looked up and copied by hand
  • The text of a buyer's question, with their name and details removed

Also worth doing: check your AI tool's privacy or data settings. Many let you choose whether your chats are used to improve their models. Settings change, so look in the app's settings menu.

The Listing Brief method

Generic AI output goes wrong for one reason: it is given too little to work with, so it fills the gaps with guesses. That is where invented materials, wrong sizes, American spellings and "stunning vintage piece" come from.

The Listing Brief fixes that. It is a short fill-in block of facts about one item: what it is, brand, size, measurements, colour, material, condition and flaws, what is included, platform, postage and your price.

Every prompt in this kit:

  1. Starts from your brief. You fill it in once and reuse it for every platform and every prompt.
  2. Uses only facts from the brief. The AI is told not to add, assume or improve anything.
  3. Marks gaps with [CHECK: ...]. Instead of guessing, the AI tells you exactly what to find out.
  4. Writes in UK English, with UK sizes and UK words.
  5. Stays within the platform's limits, and reminds you to check the current rules.
  6. Avoids hype and misleading claims.

The brief takes about two minutes. It saves more than that on every listing, and it is also what protects you if a buyer ever says the item was not as described: your listing says exactly what it was.

How to read a prompt in this kit

Every prompt has the same parts:

  • ID and name: for example T1 eBay UK title. The letter tells you the module (B brief, T titles, D descriptions and condition, K keywords, P photos, R pricing, M messages, V video, C rule checker, W workflow).
  • Use it when: one line on when it helps.
  • Paste this: the prompt. Copy all of it. Replace anything in [SQUARE BRACKETS AND CAPITALS] with your details.
  • What good output looks like: an example for an invented item, so you know what to expect.
  • Check before you post: the last few things to check yourself.

The golden rules

  1. Brief first. No brief, no listing. Two minutes of facts saves twenty minutes of fixing.
  2. Only true words. If you cannot back it up, it does not go in. That includes "rare", "vintage", "genuine", "new" and "fully working".
  3. Every flaw, with a size and a photo. Where, what, how big, which photo. If you are between two condition grades, pick the lower one.
  4. Measurements over sizes for clothing, especially vintage and pre-loved.
  5. UK English, UK sizes, UK words. Jumper, trousers, trainers, handbag, postage.
  6. No hype. No "stunning", no "must have", no capitals and exclamation marks.
  7. Only the item's own brand. No "Zara style", no "not Nike", no tagging brands it is not.
  8. Respect the limits, and check them. Platform rules change. Check the current rule in the platform's help pages, and see Module 12.
  9. Keep it on the platform. No off-platform payments, no contact details in listings or messages.
  10. Respect buyers' rights. Never write anything that tries to take away a buyer's legal rights or the platform's buyer protection.
  11. No personal data in AI tools. Items, yes. People, no.
  12. You are the editor. The AI drafts. You check every word against the item before you post.

If something goes wrong

ProblemFix
The AI invented a detailReply: "Remove anything not in my brief. Use [CHECK: ...] for gaps."
American spellings crept inReply: "Rewrite in UK English." Or use D10 in Module 03
Title is too longUse T8 in Module 02. Then check the count in the listing form
The tone is too gushingReply: "Plain, factual, no hype words, no exclamation marks."
The AI forgot the rules halfway through a long chatStart a new chat and paste the full prompt again
The free version has hit its limitTry again later, or switch to another free tool. The prompts work in all of them

Module 01: The Listing Brief

Every good listing starts here. The Listing Brief is a short block of facts about one item. You fill it in once, paste it into your AI tool, and every other prompt in this kit works from it.

Why it matters: an AI tool can only be as accurate as what you give it. Give it "blue jumper, good condition" and it will fill the gaps with guesses. Give it a proper brief and it has nothing to guess.

The one habit that makes this work: every prompt tells the AI to use only the facts in your brief, and to write [CHECK: ...] wherever something is missing. You then fill in the checks yourself. No invented details, no surprises for the buyer.

How to fill in a brief (in about 2 minutes)

  1. Have the item in front of you, plus a tape measure.
  2. Copy the brief that matches your item (general, or one of the category versions below).
  3. Fill in what you know. Leave a line blank if you do not know it. Do not guess.
  4. Write flaws in plain words: where, what, how big. "Small pale mark on left cuff, about 5mm" is perfect.
  5. Save it in your notes app. You can reuse the same brief for every platform.

Tip: blank is better than wrong. A blank line becomes a [CHECK: ...] you can fix. A wrong line becomes a "not as described" return.

Privacy tip: a brief is about the item, never about people. Do not paste buyers' names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, order numbers or messages into an AI tool. If you need help with a buyer message, replace their details with [BUYER] first.

The master Listing Brief (general)

Copy this block into your notes app and keep it as your template.

LISTING BRIEF
Platform(s): [EBAY UK / VINTED / DEPOP / ETSY / AMAZON UK / TIKTOK SHOP]
What it is (plain words): 
Brand / maker: 
Model, style name or product number: 
Category: 
Size (as on the label): 
Measurements (cm): 
Colour (as you would describe it): 
Material / composition (from the label): 
Condition (one word): New with tags / New without tags / Excellent / Very good / Good / Fair
Flaws (where, what, how big): 
What is included (box, cables, manual, dust bag, spare buttons): 
What is NOT included: 
Age or era (only if known): 
Where it came from (only if relevant and true, e.g. "bought new from the brand in 2023"): 
Smoke-free / pet-free home (only if true): 
Postage (service and who pays): 
Price I want: 
Lowest I will accept (private, never shared): 
Anything else a buyer would ask:

The "lowest I will accept" line is for the pricing and offer prompts later in the kit. Every prompt that writes buyer-facing copy is told never to reveal it.

Category brief variants

Use the general brief for anything. Use a category version when you want the AI to ask the right questions for that type of item. Each variant adds the facts buyers in that category care about most.

Clothing, shoes and accessories

For clothes, measurements beat sizes. Size 12 from a high street shop in 2024 is not the same as a size 12 from 1985, and vintage sizing runs small. Measure flat, in centimetres, and say how you measured.

CLOTHING BRIEF
Platform(s): 
Item type (e.g. jumper, midi dress, straight-leg jeans): 
Brand: 
Size on label (UK / EU / US as printed): 
Fits like (only if you have tried it or compared it): 
Measurements, laid flat (cm):
  Pit to pit (armpit to armpit, across the front): 
  Length (top of shoulder by the collar to hem): 
  Sleeve (shoulder seam to cuff): 
  Waist (straight across, doubled if you want full waist): 
  Inside leg (crotch seam to hem): 
  Rise (crotch seam to top of waistband): 
  Hips / hem width: 
Colour: 
Fabric (copy the care label, e.g. 80% wool, 20% polyamide): 
Fit / cut (e.g. oversized, slim, cropped, high waisted): 
Pattern / details (buttons, pockets, lining, zip type): 
Condition: 
Flaws (bobbling, marks, pulls, fading, stretched cuffs, missing buttons, odour): 
Tags attached? (yes / no / cut label): 
Era (only if known, e.g. "tag style suggests 1990s" is fine, a guessed year is not): 
Smoke-free / pet-free home (only if true): 
Postage: 
Price: 
Lowest I will accept (private):

How to measure pit to pit: lay the item flat, buttoned or zipped, smooth it without stretching, and measure straight across from one armpit seam to the other. Double it for an approximate chest circumference, and say you have doubled it.

Tip: never describe electronics as "fully working" unless you have tested every function. "Tested and working: power, screen, Wi-Fi, speakers. Not tested: Bluetooth" is honest and protects you.

Tip: run a fingertip round the rim of any glass or china and hold it up to the light. Hairline cracks and tiny chips are the most common cause of "not as described" claims in homeware.

Tip: for handmade items, be careful with safety and health wording. "Soothing" candles and "healing" crystals are health claims. Describe what the item is and what it is made from, not what it does to the body.

The B prompts

These prompts help you build a brief from whatever you have: scribbled notes, a voice note, a photo description, or a product label. The AI's only job here is to organise facts and flag gaps. It does not write the listing yet.

B1 Messy notes to Listing Brief

Use it when: you have jotted down a few scrappy notes about an item and want them turned into a tidy brief. Paste this:

You are helping a UK second-hand seller organise facts about one item. Turn my notes below into a Listing Brief using exactly these headings:

Platform(s), What it is, Brand / maker, Model or style, Category, Size (as on label), Measurements (cm), Colour, Material, Condition, Flaws, What is included, What is not included, Age or era, Postage, Price, Anything else.

Rules:
1. Use UK English spelling and vocabulary (colour, jumper, trousers, postage).
2. Use ONLY facts that are in my notes. Do not add, assume or improve anything.
3. If a heading has no information, write [CHECK: what I need to find out]. Be specific, e.g. [CHECK: measure pit to pit in cm].
4. Keep my flaw descriptions exactly as serious as I wrote them. Do not soften or remove any flaw.
5. Convert inches to cm only if I gave inches, and show both (e.g. 21 in / 53 cm).
6. No sales language. This is a fact sheet, not an advert.
7. At the end, list the 3 most important [CHECK] items a buyer in this category would ask about.

My notes:
[PASTE YOUR NOTES HERE]

What good output looks like:

For the notes "grey next jumper sz12 wool mix, bit bobbly under arms, vinted, want 12 quid":

Platform(s): Vinted What it is: Jumper Brand / maker: Next Model or style: [CHECK: style, e.g. crew neck, V-neck, roll neck] Size (as on label): 12 Measurements (cm): [CHECK: measure pit to pit, length and sleeve, laid flat] Colour: Grey Material: Wool blend [CHECK: exact composition from the care label] Condition: [CHECK: choose one word, e.g. Good] Flaws: Some bobbling under the arms Price: £12 ... Top 3 checks: exact fabric composition, measurements, whether there are any marks or holes besides the bobbling.

Check before you post:

  • Fill in every [CHECK] with a real fact, or delete the line if it does not apply.
  • Make sure the AI has not quietly upgraded your wording (for example "wool mix" becoming "merino").
  • Keep your lowest price out of anything a buyer will see.

B2 Voice note transcript to Listing Brief

Use it when: you talked about the item into your phone's voice recorder (quicker than typing) and have the transcript. Paste this:

Below is a transcript of me talking about an item I am selling in the UK. It will be rambling, with "um", repeats and corrections. Turn it into a Listing Brief.

Headings: Platform(s), What it is, Brand / maker, Model or style, Size, Measurements (cm), Colour, Material, Condition, Flaws, What is included, What is not included, Tested (how), Postage, Price, Anything else.

Rules:
1. UK English.
2. Where I corrected myself ("no wait, it's a 14"), use the correction only.
3. Use ONLY facts I actually said. Do not fill gaps with typical details for this type of item.
4. If something is missing or unclear, write [CHECK: ...] and say what was unclear.
5. Voice transcription often mishears brand names and numbers. If a brand, model number or measurement looks odd, keep it but add [CHECK: transcript said "X", confirm spelling].
6. Keep every flaw I mentioned, at the same level of seriousness.
7. No sales language.

Transcript:
[PASTE TRANSCRIPT HERE]

What good output looks like:

For a transcript that includes "it's a Dualit toaster, um, four slice, cream, works fine, I did two rounds of toast, there's a little dent on the back, no, the side, left side, and the crumb tray's a bit stained":

What it is: Four-slice toaster Brand / maker: Dualit [CHECK: model name or number from the base label] Colour: Cream Tested (how): Toasted two rounds of bread Flaws: Small dent on the left side [CHECK: size in mm or cm]. Crumb tray has some staining. What is included: [CHECK: is the crumb tray the only removable part? Any manual or box?] Anything else: [CHECK: plug type, assume nothing]

Check before you post:

  • Brand names and model numbers are the words transcription gets wrong most often. Check them against the label.
  • Confirm the corrected details (left side, not back) are the ones that made it in.
  • Photograph any flaw the brief mentions.

B3 Photo description to Listing Brief

Use it when: you want to describe what you can see in your photos (or on the item) and turn it into a brief. This prompt does not need the AI to see images, so it works in any free tool. Paste this:

I am going to describe my item photo by photo, as if I am showing it to you. Build a UK Listing Brief from my descriptions only.

Headings: What it is, Brand / maker, Model or style, Size, Measurements (cm), Colour, Material, Condition, Flaws (with location), Labels and markings (copy exact wording), What is included, Postage, Price.

Rules:
1. UK English.
2. Use only what I describe. Do not guess brand, age, material or value from the type of item.
3. For each flaw, record where it is and how big, if I said so. If I did not give a size, add [CHECK: size of flaw].
4. After the brief, give me a list of any extra photos a buyer would expect to see that I have not described (for example care label, base stamp, flaw close-up).
5. No sales language.

My photo descriptions:
Photo 1: [DESCRIBE]
Photo 2: [DESCRIBE]
Photo 3: [DESCRIBE]
Price: [PRICE]
Postage: [POSTAGE]

What good output looks like:

For a ceramic jug described across three photos:

What it is: Ceramic milk jug Brand / maker: Base stamp reads "Denby, Made in England" (copied as described) Colour: Blue glaze outside, cream inside Measurements (cm): 12 cm tall [CHECK: width including handle] Flaws: Tiny glaze chip on the rim, next to the spout [CHECK: size in mm] Labels and markings: "Denby, Made in England" Extra photos to take: close-up of the rim chip with a coin or ruler for scale, inside of the jug, base stamp in focus.

Check before you post:

  • If you are unsure a stamp is genuine, describe what it says rather than stating who made it.
  • Take the extra flaw photos the AI lists. A flaw shown in a photo is much harder to dispute.
  • Confirm measurements with a tape, not by eye.

B4 Gap finder: what a buyer will ask

Use it when: you have a brief and want to catch the questions buyers will message you about, before they ask. Paste this:

Here is a Listing Brief for an item I am selling on [PLATFORM] in the UK. Act as a careful, fussy buyer in this category.

1. List up to 8 questions a serious buyer would ask before buying, most important first.
2. For each, say whether my brief already answers it (Yes / No / Partly).
3. For every No or Partly, tell me exactly what to check or measure, in plain words, and how to do it quickly.
4. Do not write the listing. Do not invent answers.
5. UK English, short lines, suitable for reading on a phone.

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

What good output looks like:

For a pair of Levi's 501 jeans on eBay UK:

QuestionAnswered?What to do
What are the real waist and inside leg?PartlyLay flat, measure straight across the top of the waistband and double it. Measure inside leg from crotch seam to hem.
Button fly or zip?NoCheck and add.
Any wear at the crotch or hems?NoLook closely at the inner thighs and back hems. Photograph any thinning.
Is it the original hem or taken up?NoLook for a factory chain-stitch hem versus a home-sewn one. If unsure, say "unsure".

Check before you post:

  • Add the answers to your brief, not just to the listing, so every platform version gets them.
  • "Unsure" is a valid honest answer. Guessing is not.
  • If the same question keeps coming up for a category, add it to your brief template.

B5 Build my own category brief

Use it when: you sell a lot of one thing (bikes, prams, golf clubs, perfume, board games) and want a brief template tailored to it. Paste this:

I sell second-hand [CATEGORY] in the UK on [PLATFORM(S)]. Create a reusable Listing Brief template for this category.

Include:
1. The general fields: platform, what it is, brand, model, size or dimensions, colour, material, condition, flaws, what is included, postage, price, lowest I will accept (private).
2. Up to 10 extra fields that buyers of this category specifically care about, with a short hint in brackets on how to find each fact (e.g. "frame size (printed on the seat tube)").
3. A short "safety and legal" note listing anything I should check before selling this category in the UK, phrased as questions for me to check with the platform's help pages. Do not state rules as fact.

Rules: UK English, plain words, no sales language, formatted as a plain text block I can copy into my notes app.

What good output looks like:

For children's car seats:

CAR SEAT BRIEF ... Safety standard label (copy the exact wording from the orange or white label on the seat): Group / size range on the label (e.g. height range in cm): Date of manufacture (usually moulded into the plastic shell): Ever been in a vehicle collision? (yes / no / unknown): Isofix or belt fitted: Covers washed? (yes / no): ... Safety and legal questions to check: Does the platform allow second-hand car seats in this category? Are there any rules on seats with no known history?

Check before you post:

  • Some categories are restricted or banned on some platforms. Check the platform's prohibited and restricted items page before listing.
  • Save the template and use it for every item in that category.
  • If a field does not apply to one item, delete it rather than leave it blank in the listing.

B6 Label or box text to Listing Brief

Use it when: you have a new or boxed item (or a clear product label) and want to pull the facts off it accurately. Paste this:

Below is text I have copied from the box, label or manual of an item I am selling in the UK. Extract a Listing Brief from it.

Headings: What it is, Brand, Model / product number, Specification (list), Colour, Material, Dimensions, What is in the box, Safety or age warnings (copied exactly), Condition, Flaws, Postage, Price.

Rules:
1. UK English.
2. Copy technical specifications exactly as written. Do not round, convert or "tidy" numbers.
3. Do not include marketing claims from the box (e.g. "best ever", "clinically proven") as facts. Leave them out and list them separately under "Box claims I have not included" so I can decide.
4. Condition, flaws, postage and price are not on the box: write [CHECK: ...] for them unless I add them below.
5. Copy any safety warnings or age guidance word for word.

Box or label text:
[PASTE TEXT]

My extra details (condition, flaws, whether opened, postage, price):
[ADD DETAILS]

What good output looks like:

For a boxed electric toothbrush:

What it is: Electric toothbrush Brand: [as printed] Model / product number: [as printed] What is in the box: 1 handle, 1 brush head, 1 charging base Condition: New, box opened to check contents, brush head still sealed Box claims I have not included: "removes up to 100% more plaque". This is a manufacturer claim. Leave it out of your listing unless you are the brand and can support it.

Check before you post:

  • Leave out health, performance and "clinically proven" style claims unless you are the brand and can back them up.
  • Check whether the item's category has hygiene rules on the platform (opened personal care items often do).
  • Photograph the box and label so buyers can read the model number.

B7 Brief tidy-up and consistency check

Use it when: your brief is filled in and you want a final sanity check before you run the title and description prompts. Paste this:

Check my Listing Brief for a UK [PLATFORM] listing. Do not rewrite it into a listing.

Report back, in this order:
1. Contradictions (e.g. condition "Excellent" but flaws listed that sound like "Good").
2. Vague wording a buyer could dispute (e.g. "small mark" with no location or size). Suggest a clearer version using only my facts.
3. Missing facts buyers in this category expect, as [CHECK: ...] lines.
4. Anything that could be a misleading or risky claim (e.g. "rare", "genuine", "fully working", "vintage" without an era, health claims). Explain why in one line each.
5. US spellings or sizes to change to UK ones.

UK English. Short bullet points. Do not invent facts to fix problems. Ask me instead.

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

What good output looks like:

For a brief for a Radley handbag:

Contradictions: Condition says "Excellent" but flaws mention "corners rubbed through to the lining". That is closer to Good or Fair. Consider changing the condition. Vague wording: "small mark inside" could become "small blue pen mark on the inside lining, about 1 cm, near the zip pocket" [CHECK: confirm colour and size]. Missing facts: [CHECK: dimensions in cm], [CHECK: strap drop in cm], [CHECK: dust bag included?] Risky claims: "100% genuine": only say this if you can back it up (receipt, bought from the brand). Otherwise just state the brand and show the labels. US to UK: "purse" to "handbag" or "bag".

Check before you post:

  • Fix contradictions in the brief itself so every platform version inherits the fix.
  • If the AI flags "genuine" or "authentic", keep the photos of labels, codes and receipts ready.
  • Run this check on your first few briefs until the habit sticks.

Quick reference: what makes a strong brief

WeakStrong
Size MSize M on label. Pit to pit 54 cm, length 68 cm, laid flat
Good conditionGood. Light bobbling under both arms. No holes or marks
Small markPale mark on front, left of the buttons, about 5 mm
WorksTested: powers on, connects to Wi-Fi, all buttons respond. Bluetooth not tested
VintageCare label and tag style suggest 1990s (not confirmed)
GenuineBrand labels shown in photos. Receipt available [only if true]
Comes with stuffIncluded: charger, original box. Not included: manual

Next step: take your finished brief to Module 02 for titles, Module 03 for descriptions and condition, and Module 04 for keywords, tags and item specifics.

Module 02: Titles

The title is the part of your listing that does the most work. It is what search matches, and on a phone it is often the only text a buyer reads before tapping (or scrolling past).

A good title is not clever. It is the words a buyer would type, in the order they would type them, with nothing untrue and nothing wasted.

Every prompt in this module starts from your Listing Brief (Module 01). If you have not made one yet, do that first. It takes two minutes and it is the difference between a title with facts and a title with guesses.

Title lengths and rules at a glance

Limits change. We checked these in September 2026, but always check the current rule in the platform's help pages before relying on it. Module 12 has the full cheatsheet with sources and dates.

PlatformTitle length (at the time of writing)Other title rulesNotes
eBay UK80 charactersUse the space for relevant keywords such as brand, model and variant. No unrelated brand namesFront-load brand and item type
VintedNo confirmed limit. Check the listing formVinted relies on its own fields (brand, size, colour, condition, material) for filtersShort, clear titles read best in the app
DepopOne combined description field (commonly quoted as 1,000 characters)The opening words act like a title in search and in the feedTreat your first line as the title
Etsy140 charactersReadable phrase first, not a list of keywordsKeep it short enough to read at a glance
Amazon UK75 characters for all categories except media, from 27 July 2026No ! $ ? _ { } ^ ¬ ¦ unless part of the brand name. No word more than twice (small words like "and" excepted). New 125-character "Item Highlights" fieldAmazon may rewrite titles that break the rules
TikTok Shop UKMinimum 15 characters. Maximum commonly quoted as 255 charactersNo promotions ("20% off"), no seller name or web address, no mention of TikTok or other platforms, no symbols or special charactersAccurate and concise: product type, material, key features, quantity, size

Spaces and punctuation count as characters on every platform. A title that is one character over will be rejected or cut off.

Title formulas by category

Use these as a starting order. Swap the order if buyers in your niche search differently (for example, collectors often search set number first).

eBay UK (80 characters)

CategoryFormula
ClothingBrand + Gender + Item type + Key style + Colour + Material + Size + (Fit or detail)
ShoesBrand + Model + Gender + Shoe type + Colour + UK size + (Material)
ElectronicsBrand + Model name + Model number + Capacity or spec + Colour + (Unlocked / Boxed)
BooksTitle + Author + Format + (Edition, only if confirmed) + Year of this copy
Vinyl and CDsArtist + Title + Format + (Label, catalogue number) + (Pressing, only if confirmed)
HomewareBrand or maker + Range or pattern + Item type + Colour + Size or capacity
Toys and collectablesBrand + Name or set number + Series + (Complete / Boxed) + Year if printed

Vinted and Depop (short, style-led)

CategoryFormula
ClothingBrand + Item type + Colour + Size + (One style word buyers use, e.g. "oversized")
ShoesBrand + Model + Colour + UK size
AccessoriesBrand + Item type + Colour + (Material)
Homeware and books (Vinted)Brand or title + Item type + Key detail

Etsy (140 characters, readable first)

TypeFormula
HandmadeWhat it is in plain words + Main material + Key feature + (Personalisation) + (Who or what it is for)
VintageEra (only if you can support it) + Brand or maker + Item type + Material + Colour
Craft suppliesMaterial + Item type + Size or quantity + Colour

Amazon UK (75 characters, all categories except media)

TypeFormula
Most productsBrand + Product type + Key feature + Size or quantity + Colour
Media (books, music, video)Follow the category style guide. Media is excluded from the 75-character change

TikTok Shop UK

TypeFormula
Most productsBrand + Product type + Material + Key feature + Size, colour or quantity. Plain words, no symbols, no promotions, no platform names

Title mistakes that cost you

  • Hype words: "Stunning", "Amazing", "Must have", "L@@K". They take up space and buyers do not search for them.
  • Unsupported claims: "Rare", "Vintage", "Genuine", "Limited edition", "Brand new" when it is not.
  • Other brands as keywords: "Not Zara" or "Zara style" is keyword spam and can break platform rules. List only the actual brand.
  • US words: "pants" (UK buyers search "trousers"), "sweater" (UK: "jumper"), "purse" (UK: "handbag"), "sneakers" (UK: "trainers").
  • Size confusion: say "UK 8" for shoes, not just "8". For clothes, say what is on the label.
  • Repeating words: "Dress Midi Dress Summer Dress" does not help and on Amazon it breaks the rules.

The T prompts

Each prompt ends with the same short safety block so you can see exactly what the AI has been told.

T1 eBay UK title (80 characters)

Use it when: you are listing on eBay UK and want a title that uses the space well without padding. Paste this:

Write 3 eBay UK listing titles for the item in my Listing Brief below.

How to build them:
- Put the words a UK buyer would search first: brand, then item type, then the most important details (model, size, colour, material).
- Use this order unless the brief suggests a better one for this category: [FORMULA, OR WRITE "YOUR CHOICE"]
- Aim for 70 to 80 characters. Never go over 80 characters including spaces.
- After each title, show the exact character count.

Rules:
1. UK English and UK sizes (e.g. "UK 8" for shoes, "trousers" not "pants").
2. Use ONLY facts in my Listing Brief. If a key search word is missing (e.g. model number), write [CHECK: model number] in the title and tell me.
3. No hype words (stunning, amazing, must have, wow, L@@K), no exclamation marks, no emoji, no capital letters for whole words.
4. No misleading claims: do not use rare, vintage, genuine, new, limited edition, or a date unless the brief supports it.
5. Do not mention any brand other than the item's actual brand.
6. Do not repeat words.

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

What good output looks like:

For a grey Next wool-blend jumper, size 12, light bobbling under the arms:

  1. Next Womens Grey Wool Blend Crew Neck Jumper Size 12 Long Sleeve Knit Pullover (78)
  2. Next Grey Wool Blend Jumper Womens UK 12 Crew Neck Knitted Pullover Long Sleeve (79)
  3. Next Womens Wool Blend Jumper Grey Size 12 Crew Neck Soft Knit Casual Pullover (78)

Notice: no "bobbling" in the title (flaws belong in the description and condition), no "vintage", no "stunning".

Check before you post:

  • Count the characters yourself or paste the title into the eBay form. AI tools often miscount.
  • Every word must be true. "Crew neck" only if it is a crew neck.
  • Pick the version that starts with what your buyers type first. For fashion that is usually brand.
  • Do not add "free postage" to the title if eBay already shows it. It wastes space.

T2 Vinted title

Use it when: you are listing clothes, shoes, accessories or homeware on Vinted. Paste this:

Write 3 Vinted titles for the item in my Listing Brief below.

How to build them:
- Short and clear: brand, item type, colour, size, plus one style word buyers use if it is true (e.g. oversized, cropped, high waisted, wide leg).
- Aim for about 40 to 60 characters so it is readable in the app. Keep under the limit shown on the Vinted listing form (check it when you list).
- Show the character count after each.

Rules:
1. UK English and UK sizes.
2. Use ONLY facts in my Listing Brief. Write [CHECK: ...] if something important is missing.
3. No hype words, no emoji, no exclamation marks, no "bundle deal" or pricing words in the title.
4. No misleading claims (rare, vintage, genuine, new) unless the brief supports them.
5. No other brand names (no "Zara style", "not Nike").

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

What good output looks like:

For a pair of black Levi's 501 jeans, W30 L32, faded at the knees:

  1. Levi's 501 Black Straight Leg Jeans W30 L32 (43)
  2. Levi's 501 Jeans Black W30 L32 Button Fly (41)
  3. Black Levi's 501 Straight Jeans W30 L32 (39)

Check before you post:

  • Brand, size and colour also go in Vinted's own fields. Fill those in too: they power the filters buyers use.
  • Only say "button fly" if you have checked.
  • Keep the fading in the description and condition, not the title.

T3 Depop opening line (acts as the title)

Use it when: you are listing on Depop, where the first words of the description do the job of a title. Paste this:

Write 3 options for the opening line of a Depop listing for the item in my Listing Brief below. This line works as the title, so it must say what the item is straight away.

How to build it:
- Start with brand and item type, then colour, size and one or two style words buyers really search for (e.g. y2k, 90s, cottagecore, grunge) ONLY if they honestly fit the item and my brief.
- Keep each option to one short line, under about 60 characters.
- Plain text, no hashtags in this line (hashtags go at the end of the description, see Module 04).

Rules:
1. UK English and UK sizes.
2. Use ONLY facts from my brief. Write [CHECK: ...] for missing key facts.
3. An era word (90s, y2k, 70s) must be backed up by the brief. If the brief does not support it, do not use it and tell me.
4. No hype words, no emoji spam, no exclamation marks.
5. No other brand names.

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

What good output looks like:

For a brown suede Topshop jacket, size 10, tag style suggests late 1990s (not confirmed):

  1. Topshop brown suede jacket, size 10, 90s style (46)
  2. Brown suede Topshop jacket UK 10, button front (46)
  3. Topshop suede jacket in brown, size 10, boxy fit (48)

Note: "90s style" is used rather than "90s", because the era is not confirmed. If you can confirm it, change it.

Check before you post:

  • "Style" words (y2k, 90s) should describe the look honestly. Do not claim a date you cannot support.
  • Make sure the opening line matches what is in the photos.
  • Depop's own advice is short, clear descriptions with measurements and signs of wear. Your opening line should set that up.

T4 Etsy title (140 characters)

Use it when: you are listing a handmade, vintage or craft supply item on Etsy. Paste this:

Write 3 Etsy titles for the item in my Listing Brief below.

How to build them:
- Start with a clear, readable phrase that says exactly what the item is, as a person would say it. Then add the most important details: main material, key feature, size, colour, and personalisation if offered.
- Keep under 140 characters including spaces, and ideally under 15 words.
- Do not stuff: each phrase should add a new detail, not repeat the same idea in different words.
- Show the character count and word count after each.

Rules:
1. UK English (personalised, colour, jewellery).
2. Use ONLY facts in my Listing Brief. Write [CHECK: ...] for anything missing.
3. No hype words, no "best", no "perfect gift" unless the brief states who it is designed for.
4. "Vintage" only if the brief says the item is at least 20 years old and I can support that. Check Etsy's current vintage rules.
5. No health or wellbeing claims (e.g. calming, healing, anxiety relief).
6. No other brand names or trademarked characters.

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

What good output looks like:

For a handmade sterling silver stacking ring, hammered finish, sizes J to Q:

  1. Hammered Sterling Silver Stacking Ring, Handmade Thin Band, UK Sizes J to Q (75 characters, 13 words)
  2. Sterling Silver Stacking Ring with Hammered Finish, Handmade Thin Band (70 characters, 10 words)
  3. Handmade Hammered Silver Ring, Thin Sterling Stacking Band, Minimalist (70 characters, 9 words)

Check before you post:

  • "Sterling silver" is a legal description. Only use it if it is 925 silver, and check whether your item needs hallmarking in the UK.
  • Etsy titles do not need to use all 140 characters. Clear beats long.
  • Put your extra keywords in the 13 tags (Module 04), not the title.

T5 Amazon UK title and Item Highlights

Use it when: you are a brand or seller creating an Amazon UK product listing. Paste this:

Write an Amazon UK product title and an Item Highlights line for the product in my Listing Brief below.

Title:
- Order: Brand, product type, key feature, size or quantity, colour (unless my category style guide says otherwise).
- 75 characters or fewer including spaces (the limit for all categories except media from 27 July 2026; I will check the current rule and my category style guide).
- Capitalise the first letter of each word except short words (and, or, for, the, with, in, of).
- Numbers as digits (2, not two). Units spelled clearly (cm, ml, kg).
- Show the character count.

Item Highlights (if my category has this field):
- Up to 125 characters. Extra useful details (material, use, size range) that did not fit in the title. No repetition of the title.
- Show the character count.

Rules:
1. UK English.
2. Use ONLY facts in my brief. Write [CHECK: ...] for anything missing.
3. No special characters ! $ ? _ { } ^ ¬ ¦ (unless part of the brand name) and no emoji.
4. Do not use the same word more than twice (short words like "and", "with", "for" excepted).
5. No promotional or subjective words (best, top quality, hot item, free delivery, sale, 100% guaranteed).
6. No health, medical or environmental claims unless my brief gives the evidence and I confirm it is allowed.
7. No other brands.

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

What good output looks like:

For a set of 4 invented "Hartwell Home" linen napkins, 45 cm square, sage green:

Check before you post:

  • "100% linen" and washing temperature must come from your product spec, not the AI.
  • Amazon may rewrite titles that do not meet its rules. Reading your title back as a buyer on a phone is the best test.

Use it when: you have 2 to 5 title ideas and want an honest, buyer's-eye comparison. Paste this:

For each title:

Then recommend one and explain why in two lines. Do not invent new facts. If you suggest an improved version, use only facts from the brief.

UK English.

[PASTE TITLE 3]

What good output looks like:

For three eBay titles for a Nintendo Switch Lite:

TitleCharactersMatches "switch lite grey"Matches "nintendo switch lite console"First 40 characters clear?Issues
178YesYesYesNone

How to test for real: after you post, search the platform the way a buyer would (use the app, not your seller view) and see if your listing appears for the obvious searches. If it does not, compare your title with sold listings for similar items and look at which words they share. Change one thing at a time so you know what made the difference.

Check before you post:

  • The AI's guess at buyer searches is a starting point. The platform's own search suggestions (start typing in the search bar) are a better guide.

T8 Title fixer: too long, too vague or too spammy

Use it when: you already have a title (maybe from an old listing or a generic AI tool) and it needs fixing. Paste this:

Fix this [PLATFORM] UK listing title. The limit is [LIMIT] characters (I will double-check the current limit in the platform's help pages).

My current title:
[PASTE TITLE]

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

Do this:
1. List what is wrong with it: over the limit, hype words, repeated words, US spellings or sizes, unsupported claims, other brand names, wasted words.
2. Write 2 fixed versions, each within the limit, with character counts.
3. Only use facts from the brief. If the old title claims something the brief does not support, remove it and tell me what you removed and why.

UK English. No hype, no emoji, no exclamation marks.

What good output looks like:

For the old eBay title "STUNNING!!! Vintage RARE Mulberry Style Leather Purse Bag Bag Brown L@@K" on a brown leather handbag with no brand label:

What is wrong: Capitals and exclamation marks. "Stunning" and "L@@K" are hype. "Vintage" and "rare" are not supported by the brief. "Mulberry Style" names another brand, which is not allowed. "Bag" is repeated. "Purse" is a US word for a handbag. Fixed:

  1. Womens Brown Leather Handbag, Shoulder Strap, Top Zip, Two Handles, Medium (74)
  2. Womens Brown Leather Shoulder Handbag with Top Zip, Twin Handles, Medium (72)

Removed: "Mulberry Style" (another brand's name, a keyword and trademark risk), "Vintage" and "Rare" (not in the brief).

Check before you post:

  • If the item has no brand label, do not guess one. "Unbranded" is fine and honest.
  • Update the description to match the new title so they tell the same story.
  • If the old title was on a live listing, check whether editing it affects any watchers or offers on that platform.

Title checklist (use for every listing)

Next: Module 03 for descriptions and condition, and Module 04 for the keywords, tags and item specifics that do the rest of the search work.

Module 03: Descriptions and condition

The title gets the tap. The description closes the gap between "that looks nice" and "I know exactly what I am getting". It is also your best protection against returns and "not as described" claims.

A good second-hand description is not long. It is complete. It answers the questions a buyer would ask, in the order they would ask them, and it tells the truth about flaws in plain words.

Every prompt here uses your Listing Brief from Module 01.

The shape of a good description

For most items, this order works on every platform:

  1. What it is. One line: brand, item, key detail.
  2. Size and measurements. For clothes, measurements in cm. For everything else, dimensions.
  3. Condition, with flaws. The grade, then each flaw: where, what, how big, which photo.
  4. Details. Material, features, what is included, what is not.
  5. Postage. How it will be sent, if the platform does not already show it.

Short paragraphs or short lines. Most of your buyers are reading on a phone.

The honest condition grading scale

Use this scale in your brief, then match it to the nearest option in the platform's own condition dropdown. Platforms use different names, and they change them, so always read the platform's own definitions when you pick and check the current options in its help pages.

Our gradeWhat it meansTypical flaws allowedeBay UK (pre-owned clothing options, from February 2025)Vinted options
New with tagsUnworn, unused, original tags attachedNoneNew with tagsNew with tags
New without tagsUnworn, unused, tags removed or no tagsNone, apart from possible shop marksNew without tagsNew without tags
ExcellentUsed, but hard to tellVery faint signs of use, describedPre-owned: ExcellentVery good
Very goodLight, normal signs of useLight bobbling, faint fading, tiny marks, all describedPre-owned: Excellent or Pre-owned: Good (read the definitions)Very good
GoodClearly used, fully usableVisible bobbling, small marks, light wear at cuffs or corners, all described and photographedPre-owned: GoodGood
FairWell used, flaws are obviousStains, holes, heavy wear, faults, all described and photographedPre-owned: FairSatisfactory

Other eBay categories (electronics, books, homeware) have their own condition lists. eBay publishes an "item conditions by category" help page. Check it for your category.

Two rules for grading:

  • If you are between two grades, pick the lower one. A buyer who gets better than expected is happy. A buyer who gets worse opens a case.
  • The grade never replaces the flaw list. "Good" is an opinion. "Two small pulls on the back, about 3 mm each, see photo 6" is a fact.

Flaw disclosure wording that protects you

Most "not as described" disputes come from flaws the buyer did not expect. The fix is boring and effective: describe every flaw with location, type, size and photo.

Weak (invites disputes)Strong (hard to dispute)
Minor wearLight rubbing on both heels, about 1 cm, see photo 5
Small markPale grey mark on the front, below the left pocket, about 5 mm. May wash out, not tested
Some bobblingLight bobbling under both arms and along the side seams. None on the front
A few scratchesThree fine scratches on the back casing, only visible at an angle. Screen has no scratches
Used conditionPages lightly yellowed. Previous owner's name in pen on the first page. Spine uncreased
Tiny chipChip on the rim next to the handle, about 2 mm, cannot be felt when drinking. See photo 4

Wording habits that help:

  • Say what you checked: "No holes or stains that we can see" is honest. "Perfect" is a promise.
  • Say what you did not check: "Not tested with a charger" or "Not checked for odour".
  • Point to photos: "See photo 5" helps buyers find the flaw and shows you disclosed it.
  • Do not soften: "barely noticeable" is your opinion. Give the size and let the buyer decide.

A note on "sold as seen": it does not cover a description that is wrong. Even private sellers must describe items accurately, and if you sell as a business, buyers keep their legal rights under UK consumer law whatever your listing says. Platforms also run their own buyer protection schemes. An accurate description is the protection, not a disclaimer.

Measurements over sizes

For clothing, especially vintage and pre-loved, measurements are more useful than the size label. Sizes vary by brand, by decade and after washing.

ItemMeasurements buyers want
Tops, jumpers, shirts, jacketsPit to pit, length (shoulder by collar to hem), sleeve (shoulder seam to cuff), shoulder width
DressesPit to pit, waist, length, and hips for fitted styles
Trousers, jeans, shortsWaist (flat, and doubled), inside leg, rise, leg opening, hips
SkirtsWaist, hips, length
ShoesUK size as labelled, insole length in cm if you can measure it
BagsHeight, width, depth, strap drop (top of strap to top of bag)

How to measure: lay it flat on a table, do up buttons and zips, smooth it without stretching, and measure in cm. Say "measured flat" in the listing, and say if a figure has been doubled.

The D prompts

D1 eBay UK description

Use it when: you have a title and want a clear, complete eBay UK description. Paste this:

Write an eBay UK item description for the item in my Listing Brief below.

Structure:
1. One opening line: what it is (brand, item, key detail).
2. Size and measurements (in cm, say "measured flat" for clothing).
3. Condition: the grade, then every flaw as a separate line with location, size and the photo number if I gave one.
4. Details: material, features, what is included, what is not included.
5. Postage: only what is in my brief.

Rules:
1. UK English (colour, jumper, trousers, postage, parcel).
2. Use ONLY facts from my Listing Brief. For anything important that is missing, write [CHECK: ...]. Never invent measurements, materials, dates or test results.
3. Include every flaw from the brief. Do not soften, shorten or leave any out.
4. No hype words (stunning, amazing, gorgeous, perfect, must have), no exclamation marks, no emoji.
5. No misleading claims: do not say rare, vintage, genuine, fully working, new, or smoke-free unless the brief says so.
6. Do not reveal my lowest acceptable price.
7. Do not write anything about returns, refunds or buyers' rights. I will set those in eBay's own settings.
8. Short lines, easy to read on a phone. Under 200 words.

D4 Etsy description (handmade or vintage)

Use it when: you sell handmade or vintage items on Etsy and need a description that is warm but factual. Paste this:

Write an Etsy listing description for the item in my Listing Brief below.

Structure:
1. Opening two lines: what it is and what makes it distinctive, from facts in the brief only. These lines show first, so make them clear.
2. Details: materials (all of them), size and dimensions, colours, weight if relevant.
3. Personalisation: what can be personalised, how to request it, any character limits. (Skip if not offered.)
4. Making and dispatch: made to order or ready to post, and making time, from my brief only.
5. Care instructions.
6. Safety notes from my brief (e.g. "not a toy", candle safety).
7. For vintage items: era (only as supported by the brief) and full condition with every flaw.

Rules:
1. UK English (personalised, colour, jewellery, organise).
2. Use ONLY facts in my brief. Write [CHECK: ...] for missing facts.
3. Warm, plain tone. No hype words, no "perfect gift for everyone", no exclamation marks.
4. No health, wellbeing or medical claims (e.g. calming, healing, detox, relieves anxiety, hypoallergenic) unless the brief includes supplier evidence and I confirm it.
5. Materials must be exactly as the brief says. Do not upgrade "silver-plated" to "silver" or "cotton blend" to "cotton".
6. Short paragraphs, readable on a phone.

D5 Amazon UK bullet points and description

Use it when: you are a brand or seller writing Amazon UK product bullets ("About this item") and the product description. Paste this:

Bullet points:
- Each bullet starts with a short capitalised label followed by a colon (e.g. "MATERIAL:"), then one or two plain sentences.

- Up to 5 bullets. Keep each under about 250 characters (guidance is roughly 10 to 255), and I will check my category style guide in Seller Central for the current rule.

Product description:
- 100 to 200 words, plain paragraphs, no HTML.

1. UK English.
2. Use ONLY facts from my brief. Write [CHECK: ...] for missing facts.
3. No promotional or subjective claims (best, number one, top rated, highest quality), no prices, no delivery or offer information, no references to reviews, and no refund or guarantee phrases (money back, 100% guaranteed).
4. No health, medical, environmental or "eco" claims unless my brief includes the evidence and I confirm it is allowed in my category.

D6 Condition grader

Use it when: you are not sure which condition grade to choose, or which platform option matches. Paste this:

Help me choose an honest condition grade for an item I am selling on [PLATFORM] in the UK.

Use this scale: New with tags, New without tags, Excellent, Very good, Good, Fair.
Rules for grading:
- If the item sits between two grades, choose the lower one.
- Base the grade only on the flaws and details I list. Do not assume flaws I have not mentioned, and do not ignore any I have.

Then:
1. Give the grade and a one-line reason.
2. Tell me which option in [PLATFORM]'s condition list is the closest match, but remind me to read that platform's own definition before choosing, as the options change.
3. Write a one or two line condition summary for the description, listing each flaw with location and size.
4. List anything I should check or photograph to be sure of the grade.

UK English. No softening words (barely, hardly, tiny) unless I used them, and never without a size.

Item: [WHAT IT IS]
Flaws and wear: [LIST EVERY FLAW]
Tags attached? [YES / NO]
Used or worn? [HOW OFTEN, IF KNOWN]

What good output looks like:

For a Nike hoodie with light pilling on the cuffs, a faded logo print, and one small bleach spot on the back:

Grade: Good. The bleach spot is a visible permanent mark, so this cannot be Very good. Closest Vinted option: Good (read Vinted's description of each option before choosing). Condition summary: Good pre-owned condition. Light pilling on both cuffs. Logo print on the chest has faded and has fine cracks. One small bleach spot on the upper back, about 4 mm, see photo 6. Check or photograph: the bleach spot next to a coin for scale; the logo print close up; inside the hood for marks.

Check before you post:

  • The grade and the description must agree. A mismatch is a common cause of disputes.
  • Photograph every flaw mentioned in the summary.
  • If in doubt, go one grade lower.

D7 Flaw disclosure rewriter

Use it when: you have written your flaws in a hurry and want them clear, specific and protective. Paste this:

Rewrite the flaws below so they are clear and specific for a UK [PLATFORM] listing. The goal is that a buyer knows exactly what to expect and there are no surprises.

For each flaw, write one line with:
- What it is (mark, pull, chip, scratch, fading, stain, fault)
- Where it is (use left and right as the wearer or user sees it, and say so)
- How big (in mm or cm)
- How visible (e.g. "visible from arm's length", "only visible close up", only if I said so)
- Which photo shows it, if I gave photo numbers

Rules:
1. UK English.
2. Do not make any flaw sound smaller or less serious than I described it. Do not remove any flaw.
3. If size, location or visibility is missing, write [CHECK: ...].
4. Add one honest line of what I checked and found no problems with, only if I list it below.
5. No hype or reassurance words (perfect otherwise, amazing condition apart from). Just facts.

My flaws, as I wrote them:
[PASTE FLAWS]

Things I checked and found fine:
[E.G. NO HOLES, ZIP WORKS, NO ODOUR]

What good output looks like:

For the notes "mark on the front, bit of fraying at the hem, zip a bit stiff":

  • Pale mark on the front, [CHECK: which side, and size in mm]
  • Light fraying along the bottom hem at the back, [CHECK: length in cm]
  • Zip works but is stiff to pull, especially at the top
  • Checked: no holes, all buttons present, no odour noticed

Check before you post:

  • Fill every [CHECK] with a real measurement.
  • "Left" and "right" cause confusion. Say "as worn" and point to the photo.

D8 Measurements block

Use it when: you want a neat, consistent measurements section for clothing, bags or shoes, plus a reminder of what to measure. Paste this:

Step 1: Tell me which measurements buyers most want for this type of item, and in one short line each, how to measure them flat with a tape measure. Keep it to the essentials (4 to 6 measurements).

Step 2: When I reply with my numbers, format them as a neat measurements block:
- Heading: "Measurements (laid flat, in cm)"
- One measurement per line
- If I give inches, convert to cm and round to the nearest 0.5 cm, showing inches in brackets
- If I give a doubled figure, say "doubled"
- Add the label size at the top

Rules: UK English. Never estimate or invent a measurement. If one is missing, write [CHECK: measure X]. Do not add fit advice unless I give it (e.g. "fits like a UK 10 on me").

What good output looks like:

Check before you post:

3. A line saying what the bundle does NOT include (only if I mention it).
4. Total weight or parcel size if I give it.

2. Use ONLY facts in my list. If a line is missing brand, size or condition, write [CHECK: ...] on that line.

D10 De-hype and UK-ify an AI description

Use it when: you have a description from a generic AI tool or an old listing that sounds American, gushing or over-promising. Paste this:

Rewrite this listing description for a UK [PLATFORM] buyer.

Fix:
1. US spelling and vocabulary to UK (color to colour, pants to trousers, sweater to jumper, sneakers to trainers, purse to handbag, zipper to zip, closet to wardrobe).
2. US sizes to UK where the brief gives the UK size. If only a US size is given, keep it and label it "US size".
3. Remove hype and filler (stunning, gorgeous, must have, elevate your wardrobe, timeless piece, you will love it, exclamation marks, emoji).
4. Remove or flag any claim not supported by my Listing Brief (write [CHECK: ...] after it, or remove it and tell me).
5. Keep every flaw, with location and size.
6. Keep it short and readable on a phone.

After the rewrite, list what you removed or flagged and why, in short bullet points.

Old description:
[PASTE OLD DESCRIPTION]

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

What good output looks like:

Old: "OMG this gorgeous vintage sweater is a MUST HAVE!! Timeless piece in amazing condition, perfect color for fall. Fits true to size!"

Rewrite: Cream cable knit jumper, size M on label. Measured flat: pit to pit 55 cm, length 66 cm. Very good condition, light bobbling under the arms. [CHECK: fabric composition from the care label]

Removed or flagged:

  • "Vintage": not supported by the brief (no era given).
  • "Amazing condition": replaced with the grade and the actual flaw.
  • "Fits true to size": not in the brief. Measurements given instead.
  • "Fall": US word, and seasonal wording was not needed.
  • Hype words and exclamation marks removed.

Check before you post:

  • Read the rewrite against the item one last time.
  • If the AI removed a claim you know is true, add it back with the evidence (e.g. "receipt available").
  • Run Module 09's rule checker if the item is in a category with extra rules.

Description checklist

Module 04: Keywords, tags and item specifics

Buyers do not only type into a search bar. They tap filters: size, brand, colour, condition. If your listing's fields are empty, you are missing from those filtered results however good your title is.

This module covers the "behind the scenes" parts of a listing:

  • eBay item specifics: the structured fields (brand, size, colour, style, and so on).
  • Etsy tags: 13 short phrases that help your listing match searches.
  • Depop hashtags: up to 5 relevant words at the end of your description.
  • Vinted fields and search words: Vinted relies on its own fields rather than free tags.
  • Amazon UK backend search terms: hidden keywords that buyers never see.

Every prompt uses your Listing Brief from Module 01, and every prompt tells the AI to stay honest: no brand names that are not the item's, no keyword stuffing, no invented details.

Fields and limits at a glance

These are the facts at the time of writing (September 2026). Platforms change them, so check the current rule in the platform's help pages. Module 12 has the sources.

PlatformWhere keywords liveLimit or rule
eBay UKTitle, item specifics, categoryFill in every item specific that applies. Values are commonly quoted as limited to 65 characters each (check the form)
EtsyTitle, 13 tags, attributes, category13 tags, up to 20 characters each (spaces count)
DepopDescription, hashtags, category and attribute fieldsUp to 5 hashtags. Depop says to use only relevant words, brands and tags
VintedTitle, description, and the structured fields: category, brand, size, condition, colour, materialNo free tag field. Fill in every field that applies
Amazon UKTitle, Item Highlights, bullets, backend search termsBackend search terms commonly quoted as 250 bytes (bytes, not characters). If over, the whole field may be ignored. Do not repeat title words or use other brands

What counts as keyword stuffing

Keyword stuffing is packing a listing with search words that do not honestly describe the item, or repeating words to game search. It can breach platform rules (eBay, for example, has a search and browse manipulation policy) and it makes listings look spammy to real buyers.

Stuffing (avoid)Honest (fine)
"Not Zara, similar to Mango, like H&M"The item's own brand only
"Dress dress midi dress summer dress""Midi dress" once, with other real details
Tagging "Nike" on unbranded trainers"White trainers", "lace up trainers"
"Y2K 90s 80s vintage retro" on a 2022 top"Y2K style" only if it honestly has that look
Hashtags for trends that do not fit (#cottagecore on a hoodie)Hashtags that describe the item
Hidden lists of unrelated words at the end of a descriptionA short, useful description

Simple test: if a buyer searched that word, found your item and was annoyed, it should not be there.

UK search words: say it the way UK buyers type it

Generic AI tools often default to American words. UK buyers mostly search in UK English. Where a word is used in both countries, it can be worth including both in tags or specifics (not repeated in the title).

US wordUK word buyers search
SweaterJumper
PantsTrousers
SneakersTrainers
PurseHandbag (a "purse" in the UK is a small wallet)
VestWaistcoat (a "vest" in the UK is an underwear top)
SuspendersBraces
ZipperZip
CleatsFootball boots
Diaper bagChanging bag
StrollerPushchair or pram
ComforterDuvet
FlashlightTorch
FaucetTap
Cell phoneMobile phone

K2 Etsy 13 tags

Use it when: you are listing on Etsy and want 13 honest, varied tags within the 20-character limit. Paste this:

Write 13 Etsy tags for the item in my Listing Brief below.

How to build them:
- Each tag up to 20 characters including spaces. Show the character count for each.
- Use multi-word phrases a UK buyer would actually type (e.g. "silver stacking ring" not just "ring").
- Cover different angles: what it is, material, style, colour, occasion or recipient (only if the brief supports it), and personalisation if offered.
- Do not repeat the exact title phrase in every tag. Vary the wording.
- Include UK spellings (personalised, jewellery, colour). If a US spelling is commonly searched too, you may use it in one tag at most.

Rules:
1. Use ONLY facts from my brief. Do not tag a material, style or use the item does not have.
2. No other brand names, trademarked characters or celebrity names.
3. No health or wellbeing words (healing, calming, anxiety).
4. "Vintage" only if the brief supports it and meets Etsy's current vintage rules.
5. No hype words (best, perfect, amazing).
6. Output as a numbered list. Then show the 13 tags as one comma-separated line so I can paste them quickly.

Check before you post:

  • Count tags that look close to 20 characters. Etsy will not accept a longer one.
  • "Hand forged" only if you forge it by hand. Every tag must be true.
  • Fill in Etsy's attributes (colour, material, occasion) as well. They also help your item show up.

K3 Depop hashtags

Use it when: you are listing on Depop and want 5 relevant hashtags. Paste this:

Suggest 5 Depop hashtags for the item in my Listing Brief below, plus 3 spares.

Rules:
1. Depop allows up to 5 hashtags and asks for relevant words, brands and tags only. I will check the current limit in the app.
2. Each hashtag must honestly describe the item: its type, brand (only its own brand), colour, material, fit or a style the item really has.
3. Style or era tags (y2k, 90s, grunge, cottagecore, gorpcore) only if the item honestly fits them and my brief supports it. If you are not sure, leave them out and tell me.
4. No other brand names, no trend tags that do not fit, no hashtags about price or "fast selling".
5. Lower case, no spaces, UK spelling where it matters (e.g. #jumper).
6. For each, give a one-line reason so I can decide.

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

What good output looks like:

For a brown suede Topshop jacket, size 10, 90s style:

  1. #suedejacket (what it is)
  2. #topshop (the item's own brand)
  3. #brownsuede (colour and material)
  4. #90sstyle (honest style word, era not claimed)
  5. #croppedjacket (the fit)

Spares: #buttonfront, #womensjacket, #suede

Check before you post:

  • Swap hashtags rather than add more than the limit.
  • Brand hashtags must be the item's own brand, shown on the label in your photos.
  • Fill in Depop's category, brand, size, colour and condition fields as well.

K4 Vinted fields and search words

Use it when: you are listing on Vinted and want every field filled in and the right search words in your title and description. Paste this:

I am listing on Vinted in the UK. Vinted uses structured fields rather than free tags, so help me get the fields and wording right.

Step 1. From my Listing Brief, give me the value for each Vinted field: Category (suggest the most specific path, e.g. Women > Clothing > Jumpers and sweaters > Jumpers), Brand, Size, Condition, Colour (main colour, and a second colour only if clearly true), Material.
Step 2. List 5 to 8 search words or short phrases UK buyers would type for this item. Tell me which already appear in my title or description, and suggest where the missing ones could go naturally (once each).
Step 3. Flag any word in my current title or description that is not supported by the brief, or that is another brand.

Rules:
1. UK English and UK sizes.
2. Use ONLY facts in my brief. Write [CHECK: ...] if something is missing.
3. Do not suggest repeating words or adding lists of keywords to the description.
4. Category paths change in the app. Tell me to pick the closest match I can see.

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

My current title and description (if written):
[PASTE HERE]

What good output looks like:

For black Levi's 501 jeans, W30 L32:

Fields: Category: Men > Clothing > Jeans > Straight fit jeans [CHECK: men's or women's, from the label]. Brand: Levi's. Size: W30 L32. Condition: Good. Colour: Black. Material: Cotton.

Search words: levis 501 (in title), black jeans (in title), straight leg jeans (in title), button fly jeans (in description), w30 jeans (add "W30" to title, already there), faded black jeans (could go in the description: "faded to a washed charcoal").

Flags: none.

Check before you post:

  • Choose Vinted's category from the options you actually see. They do change.
  • Match the condition field to your description (see Module 03's grading table).
  • Brand must be selected from Vinted's list where it exists, so buyers who filter by brand find you.

K5 Amazon UK backend search terms

Use it when: you are a brand or seller filling in the backend "search terms" field on Amazon UK. Paste this:

Write backend search terms for my Amazon UK product listing.

Rules:
1. The field is commonly quoted as 250 bytes (not characters). For plain letters and spaces, 1 character is 1 byte, but accented letters and some symbols use more. Stay under 240 bytes to be safe and show the count. I will check the current limit in Seller Central.
2. Separate words with spaces. No commas, no punctuation.
3. Do not repeat any word already in my title, Item Highlights or bullets (listed below).
4. Do not repeat words within the field. No plurals of words already used unless they are genuinely different searches.
5. Include: synonyms, UK and US variants (e.g. jumper sweater), common misspellings buyers really make, and uses or occasions only if my brief supports them.
6. Do NOT include: other brand names, ASINs, temporary words (new, sale, on offer), subjective words (best, amazing), or offensive terms.
7. Use ONLY facts from my Listing Brief. No uses or features the product does not have.
8. Lower case.

My title, Item Highlights and bullets:
[PASTE THEM HERE]

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

What good output looks like:

For "Hartwell Home" linen napkins, set of 4, sage green:

serviettes dinner fabric reusable washable dining kitchen flax natural textured square hemmed wedding christmas table setting

(125 bytes)

Not included: "napkins", "linen", "sage" and "green" (already in the title), and "tablecloth" (a different product).

Note: "wedding" and "christmas" are uses. Keep them only if your product is suitable and your brief supports it.

Check before you post:

  • Use a byte counter (search "byte counter" for a free one) if your terms include accented letters or symbols.
  • Remove any term that would disappoint a buyer who searched it.
  • Never add other brands, even as "compatible with" terms, unless your category rules and the facts allow it.

K6 Buyer search phrase finder (from what you see)

Use it when: you want to know how buyers actually search for your item, using the suggestions the platform's own search bar shows you. Paste this:

I am selling [ITEM] on [PLATFORM] in the UK. I typed the start of a search into the platform's search bar and copied the suggestions it showed me. I also noted the titles of a few sold listings for similar items that I looked up myself.

Using ONLY the suggestions and titles below:
1. Group the search phrases into: what it is, brand and model, size, colour and material, style, condition.
2. Tell me which phrases honestly describe MY item (using my Listing Brief). Ignore any that do not fit.
3. Suggest where each fitting phrase should go: title, item specifics or fields, tags or hashtags, or description.
4. Point out any US spellings or words, and give the UK version.

Rules: UK English. Do not invent search data or say how popular a phrase is. Do not suggest words that are not true of my item. No other brands.

Search bar suggestions I saw:
[PASTE SUGGESTIONS]

Sold listing titles I looked up:
[PASTE TITLES]

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

What good output looks like:

For a Nintendo Switch Lite on eBay UK:

PhraseFits my item?Where it goes
nintendo switch lite greyYesTitle
switch lite consoleYesTitle
switch lite with caseNo, no case includedLeave out
switch lite boxedPartly, box included but no insertsItem specifics and description: "Boxed, no inserts"
switch lite turquoiseNo, mine is greyLeave out

Check before you post:

  • Only copy suggestions and titles by hand from what you see. Do not use automated tools to collect data from platforms.
  • Suggestions change over time. Repeat this for items you sell often.
  • A search phrase only belongs in your listing if it is true of your item.

K7 Keyword stuffing checker

Use it when: you want a quick check that your title, tags or hashtags are honest and will not look like spam. Paste this:

Check my [PLATFORM] UK listing for keyword stuffing and misleading search words.

Check:
1. Any brand, character or product name that is not the item's own (including "style", "like", "similar to", "not X", "dupe").
2. Words repeated more than needed in the title, or repeated across title and backend fields where the platform advises against it.
3. Style, era or trend words not supported by my Listing Brief (vintage, y2k, 90s, designer, luxury).
4. Condition or authenticity words not supported by the brief (new, unworn, genuine, authentic, rare, limited).
5. Tags, hashtags or item specifics that do not describe the item.
6. Hidden lists of words in the description.

For each problem: quote it, say why it is a risk in one line, and give an honest replacement using only facts from my brief (or say "remove").
Then give a short verdict: "Ready to post" or "Fix first".

UK English. Do not invent facts.

My listing (title, description, tags or hashtags, item specifics):
[PASTE LISTING]

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

What good output looks like:

For a Vinted listing of an unbranded floral dress:

ProblemWhy it is a riskReplacement
"Zara style" in titleAnother brand's name to attract searches. Misleading and can break platform rulesRemove
"vintage" in descriptionBrief gives no eraRemove, or "floral midi dress"
"#reformation" hashtag (in a cross-post to Depop)Another brand#floralmididress
"dress" appears 4 times in the titleStuffing, wastes space"Floral midi dress, size 12, button front"

Check before you post:

  • Using another brand's name to attract buyers can breach platform rules and trademark rules. Remove it even if other sellers do it.
  • Run this check on older listings too. They may have been written before you started using briefs.
  • Honest listings with fewer words are better than long ones with wrong words.

K8 UK and US search word pairs for my category

Use it when: you sell a category where UK and US words differ and want a reference list for your tags, specifics and backend fields. Paste this:

I sell second-hand [CATEGORY] in the UK on [PLATFORM(S)]. Make me a reference table of search words for this category.

Columns: UK word | US or other word buyers might also use | Notes (where UK and US meanings differ, and could confuse a buyer).

Rules:
1. Up to 20 rows, most useful first.
2. Flag any word that means something different in the UK (e.g. vest, pants, purse, jumper dress) so I do not mislead a UK buyer.
3. Suggest where each word should go: title (UK word only), tags, hashtags or backend fields (either), or nowhere.
4. UK English. Do not include brand names.
5. Do not claim how popular any word is. I will check the platform's own search suggestions.

What good output looks like:

For baby and toddler gear:

UK wordAlso usedNotesWhere

PramBaby carriage"Pram" in the UK often means a lie-flat carrycot styleOnly if it is a pram

DummyPacifierTags
