- Only use facts from the brief. Write [CHECK: ...] where anything is missing. Never invent materials, certifications, dimensions or safety standards.
- No health or medical claims (cure, heal, treat, prevent, relieve, detox, anti-bacterial unless certified and I say so), no "clinically proven", no "best", no comparisons with named brands, no guarantees, no fake urgency, no mention of other platforms or payment outside TikTok Shop.
- Avoid vague green claims ("eco-friendly", "sustainable") unless the brief gives a specific, checkable fact (for example "made from FSC-certified bamboo" with the certificate details).
- Plain, friendly UK tone. No hype words, no emojis unless I ask.
- After the description, list every phrase you think could count as a claim so I can check it.

What good output looks like:

Invented example: Tidy Nook bamboo drawer organiser set.

Six bamboo boxes in three sizes for sorting cutlery, utensils, stationery or make-up in drawers.

  • Three sizes: mix and match the boxes to fit your drawer layout.
  • Bamboo with a natural finish: a smooth, light wood look.
  • Separate boxes: move them around or use them in different drawers.
  • Raised edges: help keep small items in their own section.

What's included: 6 boxes (2 small, 2 medium, 2 large).

Size and specs: small 15 x 7.5 x 5 cm, medium 22.5 x 7.5 x 5 cm, large 30 x 7.5 x 5 cm. Material: bamboo [CHECK: is there a lacquer or coating?].

Care: wipe clean with a damp cloth. Do not soak.

Phrases to check: "help keep small items in their own section" is a mild functional statement. Keep it only if it is true in your own testing.

Check before you post:

  • Measure the product yourself and match the numbers to the listing exactly.
  • Remove every [CHECK: ...] by filling in the real fact.
  • If you mention a certification (for example FSC), keep the proof handy in case TikTok Shop or a buyer asks.

V6 TikTok Shop claims check and safe rewrite

Use it when: you have written (or been sent) product copy or a video script and want to catch risky claims before TikTok Shop or a buyer does.

Paste this:

You are a careful UK compliance reviewer for TikTok Shop UK product listings and short videos. Write in UK English.

Here is the copy or script to check:
[PASTE TITLE, DESCRIPTION, CAPTION OR VIDEO SCRIPT]

Here is my Listing Brief (the facts I can back up):
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF]

Go through the copy line by line. Make a table with: Original wording, Why it might be a problem, Safer rewrite.

Flag anything that:
- makes or implies a health or medical claim (cure, heal, treat, prevent, relieve, detox, boosts immunity, pain relief, anti-ageing results);
- makes a result or performance claim not supported by the brief;
- uses "best", "number one", "better than", or compares with a named brand;
- uses fake urgency or scarcity, or a discount that is not real;
- uses vague green or safety claims (eco-friendly, non-toxic, 100% safe, chemical-free) without a specific fact in the brief;
- mentions TikTok or another platform in a product title, or points buyers to pay or order elsewhere;
- uses symbols, promo wording or a shop URL in the product title;
- states a fact that is not in the brief (mark these [CHECK: ...]).

Then give me the full cleaned-up version. Only use facts from the brief. Do not add new claims while rewriting. This is a helpful check, not legal advice.

What good output looks like:

Invented example: a lavender wheat bag.

Original wordingWhy it might be a problemSafer rewrite
"Relieves back pain and helps you sleep"Health claim: implies it treats a medical condition"Microwaveable wheat bag with dried lavender. Warm it up for a cosy feel."
"100% natural and totally safe"Vague safety claim, not in the brief"Filled with wheat and dried lavender. Cotton cover." [CHECK: cover material]
"Only 3 left!!!"Possible fake urgency, symbolsRemove, or state real stock in Seller Center only
"Better than the high street ones"Comparison not supportedRemove

Cleaned-up version: Microwaveable wheat bag with dried lavender and a cotton cover [CHECK: cover material]. Warm it up for a cosy feel. Heat as shown on the care label. [CHECK: heating time and safety instructions from the label]

Check before you post:

  • For anything heated, electrical, for children or worn on skin, check the category rules in Seller Center: some need extra documents or are restricted.
  • Include the real safety and heating instructions from the product label, word for word.
  • If in doubt, leave the claim out.

V7 Live-selling run-sheet

Use it when: you are planning a TikTok Shop LIVE (or any live selling session) and want a calm, honest plan to follow, without showing your face.

Paste this:

You are helping a UK seller plan a faceless live selling session (hands and products only, voice or on-screen text). Write in UK English.

Session length: [30 / 45 / 60] minutes
Platform: [TIKTOK SHOP LIVE / OTHER]
Products (paste a short Listing Brief for each, or name, price, key facts and flaws):
[PASTE PRODUCTS]
Any real offer I am running (only if genuine): [E.G. "BUY 2 GET FREE POSTAGE" OR "NONE"]

Create a run-sheet as a table with: Time, Segment, What is on camera (hands-only or product-only), What I say or show on screen, Notes.

Include:
- A 2-minute welcome that says what we are showing today and how to buy (through the platform's own checkout only).
- One segment per product: show it, give the key facts, show flaws or limits honestly, show size or scale, say the price.
- A "questions" slot every 10 to 15 minutes.
- A 2-minute wrap-up.

Also give me:
- 6 short, honest answers to common live questions (size, postage time, returns, "is it genuine", "can you do cheaper", "can I pay another way"). Returns answers must respect UK consumer rights and the platform's return policy. The payment answer must say we only take payment through the platform.
- A list of things NOT to say on the live: health or medical claims, "best", fake countdowns or fake stock levels, invented discounts, other platform names, asking viewers to pay or message off the platform.

Only use facts from what I pasted. Write [CHECK: ...] for anything missing.

What good output looks like:

Invented example: 30-minute live, three kitchen products.

TimeSegmentOn cameraWhat I say or showNotes
0:00 to 2:00WelcomeThree products on a clean worktop"Evening. Tonight: a bamboo drawer set, a spice rack and a set of jar labels. Buy through the shop basket below."Pin the first product
2:00 to 9:00Drawer setHands lay out the 6 boxesSizes, bamboo, what's included, priceShow the tape measure on each size
9:00 to 11:00QuestionsProduct stays in shotAnswer from the Q&A listRead comments aloud, never usernames with personal details
...............
28:00 to 30:00Wrap-upAll three products"Everything is in the shop basket. Thanks for watching."

Sample answer: "Can I pay by bank transfer?" "We only take payment through the TikTok Shop checkout. It keeps you covered."

Check before you post:

  • Film a 30-second test first and check nothing personal is in shot or audible.
  • Any offer you mention must be set up for real in Seller Center before you go live.
  • Keep the "do not say" list on a sticky note next to your phone.

V8 Turn one listing into a week of short videos

Use it when: you want a few different short videos for the same item or product without repeating yourself or stretching the truth.

Paste this:

Write in UK English.

Here is my Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF]

Give me 5 different faceless short video ideas for this item, each 10 to 20 seconds. Use these angles:
1. "What you get" (unboxing or laying out contents).
2. "Size check" (next to everyday objects or a tape measure).
3. "Details close-up" (label, stitching, material, texture, ports, fixings).
4. "Honest condition" (shows any flaws in the brief and explains them calmly).
5. "How it is packed" (folded or wrapped, into the parcel).

For each idea give: a hook line (maximum 8 words), 3 to 4 shots (hands or item only), one line of on-screen text per shot, and a caption under 150 characters.

Rules: only facts from the brief; [CHECK: ...] for anything missing; no hype, no "best", no health claims, no fake urgency, no faces, no trending audio suggestions I would need rights for (tell me to use the platform's commercial-use music library if I add music).

What good output looks like:

Invented example: Nintendo Switch Lite, turquoise, used, light scratches on the back, charger included, no box.

Idea 4, "Honest condition":

  • Hook: Switch Lite, turquoise. Here's the honest bit.
  • Shot 1: front of the console, screen on. Text: "Screen: no scratches"
  • Shot 2: back of the console in daylight. Text: "Light scratches on the back"
  • Shot 3: charger next to the console. Text: "Charger included, no box"
  • Caption: Used Switch Lite in turquoise. Screen clear, light scratches on the back (shown). Charger included, no box.

[CHECK: has the console been factory reset and signed out of the Nintendo account?]

Check before you post:

  • Only claim "screen: no scratches" if you have checked it under a bright light.
  • Factory reset any electronics and remove accounts before selling, and do not show serial numbers in the video.
  • Each video should still match the listing exactly.

Quick reminders for faceless video

  • Film in daylight near a window, on a plain background. Keep the colour true.
  • Hands only. Take off rings or anything personal if you would rather not show it.
  • Use on-screen text with every voiceover line so it works with the sound off.
  • Only use music from the platform's commercial-use library or royalty-free sources.
  • Never film a buyer's parcel with their name or address visible.

09 Rule checker

Run these just before you post. They take a minute and catch the things that get listings removed, accounts warned or items returned: a flaw that went missing between your notes and the description, a title that is too long, a "genuine" you cannot prove, an "eco-friendly" you cannot back up.

Important: this is not legal advice. These prompts are a practical checklist. An AI tool can spot likely problems, but it can also miss things or be wrong about a rule. Platform rules change often. For anything important, check the current rule in the platform's help pages, and for legal questions see gov.uk, Citizens Advice or a qualified adviser.

How to use this module

  1. Write your listing (modules 02 to 04).
  2. Run C1 against your Listing Brief. This is the accuracy check and it matters on every platform.
  3. Run the platform check for where you are posting (C2 to C7).
  4. If your listing mentions brands, authenticity, health, the environment or returns, run C8 to C11 as needed.

The platform facts built into these prompts were checked in September 2026. Where a prompt says "at the time of writing", that is your cue to check the platform's help pages. Even better: copy the relevant rule text from the help pages and paste it into the prompt where it says [PASTE CURRENT RULE TEXT]. The AI will then check against today's rule rather than our summary.

What the AI is told to do in every check

  • Compare the listing with your Listing Brief and flag anything added, changed or missing.
  • Flag, not fix silently. You see every issue and decide.
  • Rate each issue: Must fix (likely to break a rule or mislead a buyer), Should fix (weak or risky) or Fine.
  • Write [CHECK: ...] where it cannot tell.
  • Use UK English and plain words.

C1 Accuracy check: listing against brief

Use it when: every time, on every platform, before you post. Paste this:

Check my listing for accuracy against my Listing Brief. You are a careful proofreader, not a copywriter. Do not rewrite the listing unless I ask.

My Listing Brief (the facts):
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

My listing (title, description, item specifics or tags, condition, price and postage):
[PASTE YOUR LISTING HERE]

Check and report, as a short list:
1. Added facts: anything in the listing that is NOT in the brief (for example a material, a size, a year, "original box", "never worn"). These are invented until I confirm them.
2. Changed facts: anything that differs from the brief (size, colour, measurements, condition, what is included, price, postage).
3. Missing flaws: every flaw in the brief must appear in the listing, worded no more mildly than in the brief. List any that are missing or softened.
4. Missing essentials: anything a buyer would need that is in the brief but not the listing (measurements, what is included, postage).
5. Misleading wording: anything that could give a false impression, even if technically true (for example "like new" for an item with wear in the brief).
6. UK English: any American spellings or sizes (for example "color", "pants" for trousers, US sizes without the UK size).

Label each point Must fix, Should fix or Fine. Finish with a one-line verdict: "Ready to post" or "Fix first".

Rules: UK English. Only compare what I have pasted. If you are unsure, write [CHECK: ...]. Do not add new selling points.

What good output looks like:

Item: grey Next wool-blend jumper, size 12, small bobbling under arms.

  1. Must fix: listing says "100% wool". The brief says "wool blend". [CHECK: care label]
  2. Fine: size, colour and price match.
  3. Must fix: the bobbling under the arms is missing from the description.
  4. Should fix: the brief has pit to pit 50 cm and length 62 cm, the listing has no measurements.
  5. Must fix: "excellent condition" does not fit an item with bobbling. Suggest "good used condition" to match the brief.
  6. Fine: UK spellings throughout.

Verdict: Fix first.

Check before you post:

  • Every Must fix is fixed, not just noted.
  • Any "added fact" you keep is one you have checked on the item itself.

C2 eBay UK pre-post check

Use it when: you are about to post on eBay UK. Paste this:

Check my eBay UK listing before I post. Report problems, do not rewrite unless I ask.

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

My listing (title, item specifics, condition, description, photos described in a line each, price, postage, returns):
[PASTE YOUR LISTING HERE]

I sell as a: [PRIVATE SELLER / BUSINESS SELLER]

Current rule text I copied from eBay's help pages today (optional but best):
[PASTE CURRENT RULE TEXT OR "NONE"]

Check against these points (our summary at the time of writing, September 2026; where my pasted rule text differs, follow the pasted text):
- Title is 80 characters or fewer, including spaces. Count it and show the count.
- Title is plain words that describe the item: no ALL CAPS shouting, no "L@@K", no hype, no unrelated brand names, no keyword lists.
- No brand comparisons or lookalike wording ("style", "like", "inspired by", "dupe") next to a brand the item is not made by. eBay's rules say "dupe" with a brand name is not allowed and comparisons with other products are not allowed.
- Nothing suggests counterfeit, replica or fake items.
- Item specifics match the brief and are not stuffed with extra keywords.
- Condition chosen matches the brief, and the description describes every flaw.
- Photos: of the actual item, no stock photos for used items, no added text, borders or watermarks.
- No request to pay, message or buy outside eBay, and no contact details (email, phone, social handles, websites).
- Returns wording: if I am a business seller, it must not say or imply buyers have no rights (for example "no returns, no refunds under any circumstances").

Output: a numbered list of issues labelled Must fix, Should fix or Fine, then the title character count, then a one-line verdict.

Rules: UK English. Only judge what I pasted. If a rule is unclear or may have changed, write [CHECK: eBay help pages] rather than stating it as fact. This is a checklist, not legal advice.

What good output looks like:

Item: Clarks black leather Chelsea boots, UK 6.

  1. Must fix: title is 86 characters. Suggested cut: remove "Womens Ladies" duplication. New count 74.
  2. Must fix: description says "Dr Martens style". These are Clarks, so remove the other brand name.
  3. Should fix: item specific "Colour" says "Black Brown Tan". The brief says black only.
  4. Fine: heel scuff described and photographed.
  5. Fine: no contact details or off-eBay wording.

Title count: 86 (limit 80). Verdict: Fix first.

Check before you post:

  • Title count is 80 or fewer after your edits.
  • No other brand's name appears anywhere unless it is genuinely relevant and allowed (check the current rule).

Look for these types of claim:
1. Health and medical: cures, treats, prevents, heals, relieves, soothes a condition, boosts immunity, detox, weight loss, "hypoallergenic", "antibacterial", "safe for babies".
2. Environmental: eco-friendly, sustainable, green, biodegradable, compostable, plastic-free, carbon neutral, "natural", "non-toxic". In the UK, environmental claims should be truthful, clear, specific and backed by evidence. Vague terms like "eco-friendly" are risky on their own.
3. Authenticity and origin: genuine, authentic, 100% real, original, handmade (if not made by the seller), vintage (without an age), "made in [COUNTRY]", "designer".
4. Quality and safety: waterproof, unbreakable, "tested", "certified", "CE marked", "UKCA", "BPA-free", "fire resistant".
5. Popularity and urgency: best seller, most popular, "everyone loves it", "only 1 left" (if untrue), "selling fast", "price going up".
6. Condition: "like new", "perfect", "flawless", "as new", "mint" (if the brief lists any wear).

For each claim found: quote it, name the type, rate it Must fix or Should fix, and suggest a replacement. If I have listed evidence that supports a claim, say it can stay, but tell me to keep the evidence and word it specifically (for example "Cotton, 100%, per care label" rather than "natural").

Rules: UK English. Do not invent evidence. Do not suggest a claim is fine just because it is common. This is a checklist, not legal advice.

What good output looks like:

Item: second-hand Joules wellies, UK 5, small scuff on toe.

ClaimTypeRatingSafer wording
"100% waterproof"QualityMust fix"No leaks when I tested them in water" (only if you did), or remove
"Eco-friendly natural rubber"EnvironmentalMust fix"Rubber" (per the brief), no eco claim
"Genuine Joules"AuthenticityShould fix"Joules" with a photo of the brand label and inside stamp
"Like new"ConditionMust fix"Good used condition, small scuff on left toe"

Check before you post:

  • Every claim left in is one you could prove if asked.
  • Vague green words are replaced with specific facts or removed.

C9 Brands, authenticity and trademark wording

Use it when: your item is branded, looks similar to a brand, or you are tempted to write "genuine", "authentic", "style", "inspired by" or "dupe". Paste this:

Check the brand and authenticity wording in my listing.

My Listing Brief (including how I know the brand, for example label, receipt, serial number, where I bought it):
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

My listing:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING HERE]

Platform: [PLATFORM]

Do the following:
1. List every brand, designer, character, team or trademark name in the listing.
2. For each, say whether the brief shows the item is actually made by or officially licensed by that brand. If not, flag it Must fix.
3. Flag any "style", "inspired by", "look-alike", "dupe", "replica", "copy", "1:1", "mirror quality" or "same as [BRAND]" wording. Explain that selling counterfeit or replica items is not allowed on any major platform and is illegal, and that using another brand's name to attract searches is against most platforms' rules even for a non-branded item. Suggest describing the item by its own features instead (for example "black quilted crossbody bag with chain strap").
4. For "genuine" or "authentic": if the brief gives proof (receipt, authenticity card, serial number, bought from the brand), suggest stating the proof plainly instead ("bought from [SHOP] in [YEAR], receipt included"). If the brief gives no proof, suggest removing the word and relying on clear photos of labels and marks.
5. If the item is handmade and uses a character, team crest or logo, flag that I may need permission from the rights holder. [CHECK: the platform's intellectual property rules.]

Rules: UK English. Never help word a listing so that a replica or counterfeit item appears genuine. If the brief suggests the item may be fake, tell me plainly not to list it as that brand. This is a checklist, not legal advice.

What good output looks like:

Item: unbranded tan leather-look tote bag.

  1. Brands found: "Michael Kors style" in the title, #mulberry in the tags.
  2. Must fix: the brief says unbranded. Neither brand made this bag.
  3. Must fix: "style" next to a brand name, and another brand in the tags. Replace with the bag's own features: "Tan faux leather tote bag, zip top, two handles, 38 cm wide".
  4. Fine: no "genuine" claims.

Check before you post:

  • No brand name appears that did not make the item.
  • Authenticity is shown with photos and plain facts, not adjectives.

C10 Keyword stuffing check

Use it when: your title, tags or description feel crammed, or you have pasted in a list of search words. Paste this:

Check my listing for keyword stuffing and fix it with me.

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

My listing (title, tags, hashtags, item specifics or search terms, description):
[PASTE YOUR LISTING HERE]

Platform: [PLATFORM]

Flag any of these, quoting the words:
1. Words repeated in the title more than needed.
2. Brand names, character names or product types that do not describe this item.
3. Lists of search words at the end of the description ("keywords: dress gown frock party wedding summer...").
4. Tags or hashtags that describe other items, trends or sizes this item is not.
5. Misspellings added on purpose to catch searches.
6. Size, colour or condition words that contradict the brief (for example "S M L" for a single size).

Then suggest a cleaner version of the title and tags that uses only accurate words from the brief, within the platform's limits.
Platform limits I have checked today (optional): [PASTE OR "NONE"]

Rules: UK English. Only use facts from the brief. If you do not know the platform's current limit, write [CHECK: current limit]. Accurate words buyers actually search for are fine; the aim is relevance, not fewer words.

What good output looks like:

Item: Boden navy spotty midi dress, size 12, eBay UK.

  1. Repeated: "dress" appears three times in the title.
  2. Unrelated: "Hobbs Whistles" in the title. Neither brand made it.
  3. Size list: "10 12 14". The brief says size 12 only.
  4. Keyword block at the end of the description: remove.

Cleaner title: "Boden Navy Spot Midi Dress Size 12 Short Sleeve Cotton Jersey" [CHECK: is it cotton jersey? The brief says cotton only.] (61 characters)

Check before you post:

  • Every word in the title is true for this item.
  • No keyword block left in the description.

C11 UK consumer law wording check

Use it when: your listing or shop has returns, refunds or guarantee wording, or you are not sure whether you are selling as a private seller or a business. Paste this:

Check the returns, refunds and guarantee wording in my listing or shop policy against UK consumer law basics. This is a practical check, not legal advice.

I sell as a: [PRIVATE SELLER CLEARING MY OWN THINGS / I BUY TO RESELL / I MAKE ITEMS TO SELL / NOT SURE]
Platform: [PLATFORM]
My returns, refunds or guarantee wording:
[PASTE WORDING]
My listing (for context):
[PASTE YOUR LISTING HERE]

Do the following:
1. Seller status: if I said "I buy to resell" or "I make items to sell", explain that I am likely to be treated as a trader under consumer law, even on a personal account, and should check gov.uk guidance. If "NOT SURE", list the kind of factors HMRC and consumer law look at (such as buying to resell, regularity, profit motive) and tell me to check gov.uk. Do not decide for me.
2. If I am a trader, flag any wording that tries to remove or limit buyers' legal rights, such as "no refunds", "no returns under any circumstances", "sold as seen" or "buyer pays all return costs even if faulty". Explain in plain words that UK buyers from traders generally have:
   - a right to goods that are of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described;
   - a short-term right to reject faulty goods, generally within 30 days;
   - for most online orders, a right to cancel within 14 days of delivery, with some exceptions (for example personalised or made-to-order items).
3. If I am a private seller, explain that the item must still be as described, that a "no returns" policy covers change of mind only, and that platform buyer protection can still apply if the item is not as described, faulty or damaged.
4. Flag any guarantee or warranty I offer that is vague ("guaranteed quality"), and suggest a clear version or removing it.
5. Suggest fair, clear replacement wording for my status.

Rules: UK English. Never suggest wording that denies legal rights. Mark this clearly as not legal advice, and tell me to check gov.uk, Citizens Advice and the platform's current help pages.

What good output looks like:

Seller: buys clothes at car boots to resell on eBay. Wording: "Sold as seen. No returns, no refunds."

  1. Status: buying to resell suggests you are likely a trader in law. Check gov.uk guidance on selling online.
  2. Must fix: "Sold as seen. No returns, no refunds" tries to remove rights that traders cannot remove. Buyers generally keep the right to cancel most online orders within 14 days and to reject faulty goods.
  3. (Not applicable.)
  4. (No guarantee offered.)
  5. Suggested wording: "Returns accepted within 14 days of delivery. Please message me through eBay to start a return. This does not affect your statutory rights."

Not legal advice. Check gov.uk, Citizens Advice and eBay's current help pages.

Check before you post:

  • Your returns settings in the app match the wording in your listing.
  • If you are a trader, your policy does not remove any legal right.

UK consumer law basics (quick reference)

Plain summary for everyday selling. Not legal advice. Check gov.uk and Citizens Advice for the current position.

TopicPrivate sellerTrader
Item must match the descriptionYesYes
Satisfactory quality and fit for purposeNot in the same way, so describe faults honestlyYes (Consumer Rights Act 2015)
Faulty item rejected for a refundOnly if not as describedGenerally within 30 days
Change-of-mind cancellation onlineNo legal rightGenerally 14 days from the day after delivery, some exceptions
Misleading claimsCan lead to platform action and "not as described" claimsAlso against UK consumer protection law
Fake or incentivised reviewsAgainst platform rulesAgainst platform rules, and banned under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024

Environmental claims: the Competition and Markets Authority's Green Claims Code says claims should be truthful and accurate, clear and unambiguous, not leave out important information, make fair comparisons, consider the full life cycle, and be substantiated. If you cannot back a green claim with evidence, leave it out.

Tax is separate: platforms now report some sellers' sales to HMRC. That report is not the same as being a trader under consumer law, and it does not by itself mean you owe tax. Check gov.uk if you are unsure.

10 Batch workflow

Listing one item with AI is quick. Listing ten items one at a time, starting a new chat for each, is not. This module shows you how to set up one chat session that knows your shop, feed it a stack of items, and get back tidy listings you can copy straight in, or paste into a spreadsheet for a bulk upload or cross-listing tool.

The order we suggest:

  1. W1 Write your shop style instruction once. Save it in your phone's notes.
  2. W3 Turn your rough notes for the whole pile into Listing Briefs in one go.
  3. W2 Start a batch session, paste your style instruction, then feed it up to 10 briefs.
  4. W4 Get the batch back as a table or CSV.
  5. W5 Run a quick accuracy check over the whole batch.
  6. W6 to W8 Plan the week, repurpose across platforms, and refresh listings that have gone quiet.

A tip for phones: free AI chats can lose track in very long sessions. If answers start drifting (American spelling, invented details, forgetting your rules), start a fresh chat and paste your shop style instruction again. Batches of 5 to 10 items work best.

Privacy: never paste buyers' names, addresses or order details into an AI tool.

W1 Build your reusable "shop style" instruction

Use it when: you are fed up of re-explaining your shop to the AI every time. Do this once, save the result, and paste it at the start of every session.

Paste this:

Help me write a short, reusable "shop style instruction" I can paste at the start of any AI chat before I list items. Write in UK English.

Here are my answers:
- Platforms I sell on: [E.G. VINTED AND EBAY UK]
- What I mostly sell: [E.G. WOMEN'S CLOTHING SIZES 8 TO 18, SOME HOMEWARE]
- Am I a private seller or a business? [PRIVATE / BUSINESS]
- My tone: [E.G. FRIENDLY AND PLAIN, NO EMOJIS / A FEW EMOJIS OK ON DEPOP]
- How I describe condition: [E.G. NEW WITH TAGS / NEW WITHOUT TAGS / VERY GOOD / GOOD / SATISFACTORY]
- How I measure: [E.G. PIT TO PIT AND LENGTH IN CM, LAID FLAT]
- My postage: [E.G. POSTED WITHIN 2 WORKING DAYS, SMOKE-FREE HOME, PET-FREE HOME, ONLY IF TRUE]
- My returns line: [E.G. "PRIVATE SELLER: I DON'T ACCEPT RETURNS FOR CHANGE OF MIND, BUT YOU'RE COVERED IF THE ITEM ISN'T AS DESCRIBED" OR THE BUSINESS RETURNS POLICY]
- Words or things I never want: [E.G. "STUNNING", "RARE" UNLESS IT IS, EMOJIS IN TITLES]
- Anything else: [E.G. ALWAYS LIST FLAWS FIRST IN THE CONDITION SECTION]

Turn this into a numbered instruction of no more than 15 lines that starts with "You are my listing assistant for a UK shop." It must include these fixed rules:
- Use UK English spelling, UK sizes and £.
- Only use facts I give you in each Listing Brief. Never invent brand, size, material, measurements, age, condition or included items.
- Where something is missing, write [CHECK: what is missing] instead of guessing.
- Respect each platform's title and description limits. For eBay UK, keep titles to 80 characters or fewer.
- No hype words, no keyword stuffing, no misleading claims, no health or medical claims, no fake urgency, no mentions of other platforms in a listing, and never suggest payment outside the platform.
- Always state flaws clearly.
Keep it short enough to fit in a phone note.

What good output looks like:

Invented example for a private seller on Vinted and eBay UK.

You are my listing assistant for a UK shop.

  1. I am a private seller on Vinted and eBay UK. I mainly sell women's clothing (UK sizes 8 to 18) and some homeware.
  2. Use UK English, UK sizes and £.
  3. Only use facts from the Listing Brief I give you. Never invent details.
  4. If something is missing, write [CHECK: what is missing].
  5. eBay UK titles: 80 characters or fewer, most important words first. Vinted titles: short and plain.
  6. Tone: friendly and plain. No emojis. Never use "stunning", "gorgeous" or "rare" unless I say so.
  7. Condition words: New with tags, New without tags, Very good, Good, Satisfactory.
  8. Measurements: pit to pit and length in cm, laid flat.
  9. List flaws first in the condition section, clearly and calmly.
  10. Postage line: "Posted within 2 working days from a smoke-free home."
  11. Returns line: "Private seller, so no returns for change of mind. You're covered if the item isn't as described."
  12. No keyword stuffing, no misleading or health claims, no fake urgency, no other platform names, never suggest paying outside the platform.

Check before you post:

  • Only include "smoke-free" or "pet-free" if it is true for every item.
  • If you are a business seller, your returns line must reflect UK consumer rights (for most online sales, buyers have a right to cancel within 14 days). Check the platform's business seller rules.
  • Re-read it every few months, and update it if your platforms or policies change.

W2 Start a batch session (list up to 10 items in one chat)

Use it when: you have a pile of items photographed and noted, and want to list them in one sitting.

Paste this:

[PASTE YOUR SHOP STYLE INSTRUCTION FROM W1]

We are going to list [NUMBER, UP TO 10] items in this chat. Platform for this batch: [EBAY UK / VINTED / DEPOP / ETSY].

How this works:
- I will paste one Listing Brief at a time, each starting with "ITEM [NUMBER]".
- For each item, reply with: Title, Description, Condition line, [ITEM SPECIFICS FOR EBAY / TAGS FOR ETSY / HASHTAGS FOR DEPOP / NOTHING EXTRA FOR VINTED], and a list of any [CHECK: ...] items.
- Keep the same layout for every item so I can copy quickly on my phone.
- Do not carry facts from one item to another. Each item uses only its own brief.
- Do not add a price unless I include one in the brief.
- When I type "DONE", stop and wait for my next instruction.

Reply with "Ready for ITEM 1" and nothing else.

Then paste each brief, for example:

ITEM 1
[PASTE LISTING BRIEF]

What good output looks like:

Invented example, platform eBay UK, ITEM 3 brief: "Joules women's quilted gilet, navy, size 12, zip front, 2 zip pockets, light pilling on inside collar, pre-owned."

ITEM 3 Title: Joules Womens Navy Quilted Gilet Size 12 Zip Front Pockets Pre-Owned (68 characters) Description: Navy quilted gilet from Joules in women's size 12. Full zip front and two zip pockets. Pre-owned in good condition with light pilling on the inside collar (see photos). Measurements: pit to pit [CHECK: cm], length [CHECK: cm]. Posted within 2 working days from a smoke-free home. Condition line: Pre-owned, good. Light pilling on the inside collar. Item specifics: Brand: Joules. Size: 12. Colour: Blue [CHECK: eBay's colour list may use Blue for navy]. Type: Gilet. Department: Women. Closure: Zip. Outer shell material: [CHECK]. To check: measurements, outer shell material.

Check before you post:

  • Scan each item for facts that "leaked" from an earlier item (a size or brand that belongs to something else).
  • Count eBay titles (80 characters maximum). The AI's count can be wrong, so trust eBay's counter.
  • Answer every [CHECK: ...] before you list.

W3 Turn messy notes for 10 items into Listing Briefs in one go

Use it when: you have scribbled quick notes for a stack of items and want them turned into proper briefs before you start W2.

Paste this:

Write in UK English.

Below are my rough notes for [NUMBER] items, one line or short paragraph each. Turn each one into a Listing Brief using exactly these headings:
Item number | What it is | Brand | Size | Measurements | Colour | Material | Condition and flaws | What's included | Platform | Postage | Price floor

Rules:
- Only use what is in my notes. Do not guess brand, size, material, age or value.
- Where a heading has no information, write [CHECK: ...] with a short prompt of what I need to find (for example [CHECK: look at care label for material]).
- If a note mentions a flaw, it must appear in "Condition and flaws".
- Keep each brief to one short block so I can check it on my phone.
- At the end, give me one combined "to find" list grouped by item, so I can check everything in one trip to the pile.

My notes:
[PASTE YOUR NOTES]

What good output looks like:

Invented notes: "1. m&s cardi cream 14 bobbly cuffs. 2. hunter wellies green uk5 scuffed toe. 3. le creuset mug blue chip base"

Item 1 | Cardigan | M&S | 14 | [CHECK: pit to pit and length in cm] | Cream | [CHECK: care label] | Bobbling on cuffs | Cardigan only | [CHECK: platform] | [CHECK: postage] | [CHECK: price floor] Item 2 | Wellington boots | Hunter | UK 5 | [CHECK: insole length] | Green | [CHECK: material, look inside the boot] | Scuffs on toe | Boots only | [CHECK] | [CHECK] | [CHECK] Item 3 | Mug | Le Creuset | [CHECK: capacity] | [CHECK: height] | Blue | [CHECK: material, look on the base] | Chip on base | Mug only | [CHECK] | [CHECK] | [CHECK]

To find: Item 1: measurements, material. Item 2: insole length, material. Item 3: capacity, height, material. All: platform, postage, price floor.

Check before you post:

  • Check the brand label on every item before you trust the brief. Never list an item as a brand you cannot confirm.
  • Measure while the pile is out, then fill in all the [CHECK: ...] gaps in one go.

W4 Batch output as a table or CSV for bulk upload tools

Use it when: you have finished a batch and want it in a spreadsheet, or in a CSV to import into a bulk listing or cross-listing tool.

Paste this:

Take all the items we have written in this chat and put them into one table.

Columns (in this order): [PASTE THE COLUMN HEADERS YOUR TOOL OR SPREADSHEET USES, OR USE: SKU, Title, Description, Condition, Brand, Size, Colour, Material, Category, Price, Quantity, Postage]

Rules:
- One row per item. Use the exact facts already agreed in this chat. Do not add or change anything.
- Leave a cell as [CHECK] if the fact is missing. Do not guess.
- If I ask for CSV: output plain CSV in a single code block, comma-separated, with every cell wrapped in double quotes. Replace any line breaks inside descriptions with a space. Replace any double quote inside a cell with two double quotes.
- Use UK English and £ with no currency symbol in the Price column (numbers only, for example 12.50).
- After the table or CSV, list any rows that still contain [CHECK].

Output format: [TABLE / CSV]

What good output looks like:

Invented example, CSV of two items:

"SKU","Title","Description","Condition","Brand","Size","Colour","Material","Category","Price","Quantity","Postage"
"WL-014","Joules Womens Navy Quilted Gilet Size 12 Zip Front Pockets Pre-Owned","Navy quilted gilet from Joules in women's size 12. Full zip front and two zip pockets. Light pilling on the inside collar (see photos).","Pre-owned, good","Joules","12","Blue","[CHECK]","Coats and jackets","18.00","1","Royal Mail 2nd Class"
"WL-015","Hunter Wellington Boots Green UK 5","Green Hunter wellington boots in UK 5. Scuffs on the toes (see photos).","Pre-owned, good","Hunter","5","Green","[CHECK]","Boots","25.00","1","[CHECK]"

Check before you post:

  • Every bulk tool has its own template. Download your tool's template and use its exact column headers, then paste those into the prompt.
  • Open the CSV in a spreadsheet app and look at it before you upload. Check that long descriptions have not split across columns.
  • Do a test upload of one or two rows first.
  • Remember the price in the table is your decision. The AI only copies what you told it.

W5 Batch accuracy check before you post

Use it when: you have a batch of listings ready and want a second pair of eyes to spot invented details, missing flaws and rule problems.

Paste this:

Act as a careful UK listings checker. Write in UK English.

Below are my Listing Briefs (the facts) and then the listings written from them. For each item, compare the listing with its brief and report:
1. Any detail in the listing that is NOT in the brief (possible invention).
2. Any flaw in the brief that is missing or softened in the listing.
3. Title length problems (eBay UK: over 80 characters; other platforms: [CHECK: the platform's current limit]).
4. Hype words, keyword stuffing (the same word repeated, lists of unrelated brands), misleading claims, health claims, fake urgency or other platform names.
5. American spellings or US sizes where a UK one is needed.

Give one short row per item: Item number | Problems found | Suggested fix. If an item is fine, write "No problems found".
Do not rewrite whole listings unless I ask.

BRIEFS:
[PASTE BRIEFS]

LISTINGS:
[PASTE LISTINGS]

What good output looks like:

Invented example:

ItemProblems foundSuggested fix
1Listing says "100% wool" but brief says "wool blend"Change to "wool blend"
2Brief lists scuffed toes, listing does not mention themAdd "Scuffs on the toes (see photos)" to condition
3Title is 86 charactersRemove "Great" and "Look" to get under 80
4"Color" (US spelling)Change to "colour"
5No problems foundNone

Check before you post:

  • The checker can miss things too. Always read the flaws section yourself.
  • If the checker flags an invention, go back to the item, not the AI, for the truth.

W6 Weekly listing routine planner

Use it when: you want a realistic weekly plan that fits your evenings and weekends, so listing does not pile up.

Paste this:

Help me plan a weekly listing routine. Write in UK English. Be realistic, not motivational.

My situation:
- Time I have: [E.G. MONDAY AND WEDNESDAY EVENINGS 1 HOUR, SATURDAY MORNING 2 HOURS]
- Roughly how many items I want to list each week: [NUMBER]
- Platforms: [LIST]
- Where I get stock: [E.G. OWN WARDROBE, CAR BOOTS, CHARITY SHOPS, MY OWN HANDMADE ITEMS]
- What slows me down most: [E.G. PHOTOS, MEASURING, WRITING, POSTING PARCELS]
- Post office or drop-off times near me: [E.G. LOCKER AVAILABLE 24 HOURS]

Give me:
1. A day-by-day plan in a table: Day, Time, Task, Roughly how many items, Tools or prompts to use (refer to prompt IDs like W2, W4, R prompts for pricing, M prompts for messages).
2. Batch tasks together (all photos in one go, all measuring in one go, all writing in one AI session).
3. A 10-minute daily check for messages and dispatch.
4. A weekly 20-minute review: what sold, what has had no interest for a while, what to refresh or reprice.
Keep it simple enough to follow on a phone. Do not promise any sales results.

What good output looks like:

Invented example: two weekday evenings and Saturday morning, aiming for about 15 items a week on Vinted and eBay.

DayTimeTaskItemsPrompts
Saturday9:00 to 10:00Photograph and measure the week's items in daylight15P prompts, shot lists
Saturday10:00 to 11:00Notes into briefs, then list the first 55W3, W2
Monday19:30 to 20:30List the next 5, run the batch check5W2, W5
Wednesday19:30 to 20:30List the last 5, weekly review5W2, W8, R prompts
Every day10 minutesReply to messages, pack and post sold itemsM prompts

Weekly review questions: What sold? Which listings have had few views or likes for 2 weeks or more? Which items need better photos, a clearer title or a price check?

Check before you post:

  • Dispatch times you promise in listings must match the plan you can actually keep.
  • Keep a simple stock and pricing tracker (see templates/stock-and-pricing-tracker.csv) so the review takes minutes, not an hour.
  • If you are selling regularly for profit, read HMRC's guidance on trading income and the platforms' reporting rules. Check the current rules on GOV.UK.

W7 Repurpose one listing across platforms

Use it when: you have written a good listing for one platform and want versions for others without starting again.

Paste this:

[PASTE YOUR SHOP STYLE INSTRUCTION FROM W1, IF YOU HAVE ONE]

Here is my Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF]

Here is the listing I already wrote for [PLATFORM]:
[PASTE THE LISTING]

Rewrite it for: [LIST TARGET PLATFORMS, E.G. VINTED, DEPOP, ETSY]

For each platform, give me what that platform needs:
- eBay UK: title of 80 characters or fewer, description, item specifics list.
- Vinted: short plain title, description with measurements and condition.
- Depop: description that starts with the key details, plus up to 5 relevant hashtags.
- Etsy: title (plain and readable, most important words first), description, and up to 13 tags of 20 characters or fewer. Only for handmade, vintage (20 years or older) or craft supplies items.
- Amazon UK: title of 75 characters or fewer for most categories (Amazon's rule from 27 July 2026; media categories differ), an Item Highlights line of 125 characters or fewer, no banned symbols (! $ ? _ { } ^ ¬ ¦ unless part of the brand), no word more than twice, up to 5 bullet points, description.
- TikTok Shop UK: title with no symbols, promo words or platform names, and a short description of at least 30 words.

Rules:
- Only use facts from the brief. The facts must be the same on every platform. Change the format and tone, not the facts.
- Write [CHECK: ...] for anything a platform needs that is not in the brief.
- Do not mention any other platform inside a listing, and never suggest buying or paying elsewhere.
- No hype, no keyword stuffing, no misleading or health claims.
- Tell me if the item looks unsuitable for a platform (for example, not handmade or vintage for Etsy, or a used item for a new-only listing) instead of forcing it.

What good output looks like:

Invented example: vintage 1990s Levi's denim jacket, size M, mid-wash, small fade at the left cuff. Originally written for eBay UK.

Vinted Title: Vintage 90s Levi's denim jacket, size M, mid-wash Description: Vintage Levi's trucker-style denim jacket in a mid-wash, size M. Small fade at the left cuff (see photos). Pit to pit 56 cm, length 62 cm, laid flat.

Depop Vintage 90s Levi's denim jacket, size M. Mid-wash, trucker style. Small fade at the left cuff (see photos). Pit to pit 56 cm, length 62 cm. #vintagelevis #denimjacket #90svintage #levisjacket #truckerjacket

Etsy Title: Vintage 1990s Levi's Denim Jacket Size M Mid Wash Trucker Jacket Tags: vintage levis, denim jacket, 90s denim, trucker jacket, levis jacket, mid wash denim, mens denim jacket, 1990s jacket, vintage jacket, blue jean jacket, retro denim, size m jacket, levis trucker Note: [CHECK: confirm the decade from the care label or tab so the "vintage" claim is accurate. Etsy's vintage category is for items at least 20 years old; check the current rule in Etsy's help pages.]

Check before you post:

  • Cross-listing the same single item? Remove it from every other platform as soon as it sells, or you may sell it twice.
  • Check each platform's current limits in module 12 (the cheatsheet) and in the platform's help pages.
  • Only call something "vintage" if you can back up its age.

W8 Refresh a batch of quiet listings

Use it when: some listings have had little interest for a couple of weeks and you want to improve them honestly, without keyword stuffing or fake price tricks.

Paste this:

Write in UK English.

Below are [NUMBER] listings that have had little interest. For each one I have added the Listing Brief, the current title and description, how long it has been listed, and any views, likes or watchers I can see.

[FOR EACH ITEM PASTE: BRIEF / CURRENT TITLE / CURRENT DESCRIPTION / DAYS LISTED / VIEWS, LIKES OR WATCHERS]

For each item, suggest:
1. A clearer title (using words a buyer would actually search for, most important first, within the platform's limit).
2. The top 1 or 2 fixes to the description (missing measurements, unclear condition, missing brand or size).
3. Photo fixes to try (for example daylight, plain background, label close-up, flaw close-up).
4. Whether a price check is worth doing, and what sold listings I should look up myself to compare (describe the search, do not invent prices).

Rules: only use facts from the brief; [CHECK: ...] for missing facts; no keyword stuffing, no "rare" or "vintage" unless the brief supports it, no fake discounts, no misleading claims. Do not promise it will sell.

What good output looks like:

Invented example: "Blue top size 10", listed 21 days, 14 views, 0 likes. Brief says: Whistles, silk-blend blouse, cornflower blue, UK 10, no flaws.

Item 1 New title: Whistles Silk Blend Blouse Cornflower Blue UK 10 Description fixes: add the brand and fabric in the first line. Add pit to pit and length [CHECK: measure]. Photo fixes: a daylight flat lay on a plain background, plus a close-up of the Whistles label and the fabric content label. Price check: search sold listings for "Whistles silk blouse size 10" on the same platform and compare items in similar condition. Note 3 to 5 sold prices in your tracker before deciding.

Check before you post:

  • Do not relist the same item many times to game search. Check the platform's rules on duplicate listings.
  • A price drop should be real. Never raise a price just to "drop" it later.

Save these for every session

Keep these three things in one phone note so a batch session takes seconds to start:

  1. Your shop style instruction (W1).
  2. The empty Listing Brief template (see templates/listing-brief-template.txt).
  3. The column headers your spreadsheet or bulk tool uses (for W4).

11 Worked examples

Six complete examples, start to finish. Each one starts with the kind of messy notes most of us actually write, then shows the Listing Brief, the title, the description, the tags or item specifics, the price reasoning and one buyer reply.

Please read this first:

  • Every item, shop and brand-owner in this module is invented for illustration. Real brand names appear only to show how a genuine branded item would be described.
  • Every "comp" (comparable sold price) is an invented example. They show the method, not real market prices. Always look up real sold listings yourself on the platform you are using, for items in the same condition.
  • Fee figures are the ones we checked in September 2026 (see module 12). Fees change. Check the current rule in the platform's help pages before you do your own sums.
  • Nothing here predicts what you will sell or earn. The aim is a clear, accurate listing.

The prompts used are shown in brackets, so you can follow along: B (brief), T (titles), D (descriptions), K (keywords and specifics), R (pricing), M (messages).

Example 1: Vinted, knitted jumper

Messy notes (before)

white stuff jumper oatmeal cable knit 14?? bit bobbly under arms. no holes. wore it a few times. smells fine. 8 quid?

Listing Brief (B prompts)

FieldFact

BrandWhite Stuff

What's includedJumper only
PlatformVinted

Price floor£10

Note: the notes said "14??" so we checked the label before writing the brief. It says 14. The notes guessed "8 quid", but the price came later, from comps.

Title (T prompts)

White Stuff oatmeal cable knit jumper, size 14, cotton wool

Description (D prompts)

Oatmeal cable-knit jumper from White Stuff, UK size 14. Crew neck, 60% cotton and 40% wool.

Condition: very good. Light bobbling under both arms (see photo 5). No holes, marks or stretching.

Measurements (laid flat): pit to pit 54 cm, length 64 cm.

Posted within 2 working days. Happy to answer any questions.

Tags and fields (K prompts)

Vinted uses fields rather than tags: Category: Women > Jumpers and sweaters. Brand: White Stuff. Size: UK 14. Condition: Very good. Colour: Beige. Material: Cotton, Wool.

Price reasoning (R prompts)

Invented example comps (for illustration only, not real prices):

CompConditionSold price
White Stuff cable jumper, size 12, creamVery good£14
White Stuff cable jumper, size 14, grey, bobblingGood£11
White Stuff jumper, size 16, oatmealVery good£15
White Stuff cable jumper, size 14, no flawsExcellent£18

Reasoning: the closest matches (same size or neighbouring sizes, similar condition) sold between £11 and £15. Ours has light bobbling, so it sits in the middle, not at the top. Vinted does not charge private sellers a selling fee; the buyer pays the Buyer Protection fee at checkout. List at £14, accept offers down to the £10 floor. Our original "8 quid" guess would have left money on the table without being any quicker to sell.

Buyer: Would you take £8?

Title (T prompts, 140 characters maximum)

Handmade Ceramic Tealight Holder Set of 2, Sage Green Speckled Stoneware Candle Holders with Star Cut Outs

(106 characters.)

Description (D prompts)

A pair of handmade stoneware tealight holders in a speckled sage green glaze, each with small star-shaped cut-outs that let the light through.

Size: each holder is about 8 cm tall and 7 cm wide, and fits a standard tealight.

Tags (K prompts, 13 tags, 20 characters maximum each)

tealight holder, ceramic candle, stoneware holder, sage green decor, speckled pottery, star candle holder, handmade pottery, ceramic tealight, candle holder set, housewarming gift, rustic home decor, pottery gift, table centrepiece

Price reasoning

This is our own product, so we price from costs first, then sense-check against the market.

Costs (invented example figures): clay and glaze £3.20, kiln share £2.00, packaging £1.40, time (1 hour at the rate we choose) £12.00. Total before fees: £18.60.

Etsy fees (checked September 2026; check the current rules): listing fee $0.20 (about £0.15), 6.5% transaction fee on the item price plus postage, and a UK payment processing fee of 4% + £0.20. A UK Regulatory Operating Fee also applies [CHECK: current rate in Etsy's fee policy].

At £24 plus £4.50 postage (order total £28.50): transaction fee about £1.85, processing about £1.34, listing about £0.15. That is about £3.34 before the Regulatory Operating Fee. After the £4.50 postage covers the real postage cost, we keep about £20.66 against £18.60 of costs.

Invented example comps (for illustration only, not real prices): three similar handmade stoneware tealight pairs listed at £22, £26 and £28.

Reasoning: £24 covers our costs and fees with a small margin and sits within the range of similar handmade pieces. List at £24 plus postage.

Buyer reply

Buyer: Hi, would these hold a small pillar candle instead?

Reply: Hi, thanks for asking. They're made for standard tealights, so a pillar candle won't fit inside. The opening is about [CHECK: inner width] cm across. If you'd like something for pillar candles, let me know and I can tell you when I have some in the shop.

What all six have in common

  1. Facts first. Every detail in the listing came from the brief. Guesses in the notes ("14??", "i think", "RRP 17.99??") were checked or dropped.
  2. Flaws up front. Bobbling, scratches, a loose stick and a mark on the back are all stated plainly, with photo numbers.
  3. No claims we cannot prove. No "best", no "rare", no health wording, no invented reference prices.
  4. Price from like-for-like comps and real costs, not from a hunch. Your own comps should come from sold listings you look up yourself.
  5. Replies stay polite, honest and on the platform.

12 Platform cheatsheet

One quick reference per platform: title and description limits, tags, photos, the main seller fees and the rules that matter most when you write a listing.

Last checked: September 2026.

Please check the current rules yourself. Platforms change limits, fees and policies often, sometimes with little notice. Before you rely on any figure here, check the current rule in the platform's help pages (links under each table). If this sheet and the platform disagree, the platform is right.

How to read this sheet:

  • A figure on its own was confirmed from the platform's own pages when we checked.
  • "Check in the platform's help pages" means we could not confirm it from an official source. Where a figure is commonly reported by other sellers and tools, we show it in brackets as "(commonly reported: ...)" so you know roughly what to expect, but please confirm it before relying on it.
  • We are not affiliated with or endorsed by any of these platforms. This is a summary for sellers, not legal or tax advice.

eBay UK

WhatRule
Title80 characters. Put the most important words first (brand, item type, model, size, colour).
SubtitleOptional paid upgrade. Length: check in the platform's help pages.
DescriptionCheck in the platform's help pages (very long descriptions are allowed; active content such as scripts is not).
Item specificsFill in as many as apply: they help your item appear in filtered searches. Value length: check in the platform's help pages.
PhotosCheck in the platform's help pages (commonly reported: up to 24 free). Photos must show the actual item. Picture rules on size, borders, text and watermarks: check eBay's Picture policy.
Private seller feesUK-based private sellers pay no final value fee and no regulatory operating fee when an item sells, in all categories except Motors (cars, motorcycles and vehicles). 300 free listings a month, then a listing fee per listing. Fees apply for optional upgrades and for delivery to an overseas address.
Buyer Protection feeOn items from private sellers, the buyer pays a Buyer Protection fee (a small flat amount plus a tiered percentage of the item price). It does not come out of the seller's payout. Current tiers: check in the platform's help pages.
Business seller feesBusiness sellers pay a final value fee by category, a per-order fee and a regulatory operating fee, plus VAT on fees. Rates changed in early 2026: check in the platform's help pages.
Key rulesDescribe the actual item and its condition accurately. No unrelated brand names or keyword spam in titles (search and browse manipulation policy). No counterfeits or replicas. Keep all communication and payment on eBay.

Title140 characters. Etsy's own guidance favours clear, readable titles with the most important words first.
DescriptionCheck in the platform's help pages.
TagsUp to 13 tags, each up to 20 characters.
Photos and videoUp to 20 photos. Video: check in the platform's help pages (commonly reported: 1 short video of 5 to 15 seconds).
Listing fee$0.20 USD per listing or renewal (shown to UK sellers as about £0.15 and billed at the exchange rate). A listing lasts 4 months or until it sells.
Transaction fee6.5% of the sale price, including the postage you charge.
Payment processing (UK)4% + £0.20 per order.
Regulatory Operating Fee (UK)Charged on UK orders. Current rate: check in the platform's help pages.
Offsite AdsA fee on orders that come from Etsy's offsite adverts (15% or 12% depending on shop sales, capped per order; commonly reported). Check in the platform's help pages.
Key rulesEtsy is for handmade items, vintage items and craft supplies. Vintage means at least 20 years old (check the current rule). If AI was used in creating an item, Etsy's Creativity Standards ask you to say so in the description. No keyword stuffing, no counterfeits, no health or medical claims.

Amazon UK

WhatRule
Title75 characters or fewer, including spaces, in all categories except media (rule from 27 July 2026). Amazon may shorten over-length titles itself.
Item HighlightsNew field of up to 125 characters, shown below the title. Your title must be 75 characters or fewer for it to work.
Title rulesNo special characters ! $ ? _ { } ^ ¬ ¦ unless part of the brand name. The same word no more than twice (prepositions, articles and conjunctions excepted). No promotional wording.
Bullet pointsUp to 5. Length per bullet: check in the platform's help pages. No prices, delivery or company information in bullets.
DescriptionCheck in the platform's help pages (commonly reported: 2,000 characters).
Search terms (backend keywords)A byte limit applies, and going over it can mean the whole field is ignored. Check in the platform's help pages (commonly reported: 250 bytes). Do not repeat title words or use other brands' names.
PhotosMain image rules (white background, no added text or logos): check in the platform's help pages. Image count: check in the platform's help pages.
Selling plansIndividual: £0.75 per item sold. Professional: £25 a month excluding VAT.
Referral feesCharged on each sale, varying by category. Check the current rate for your category on Amazon's pricing page. Fulfilment fees apply if you use FBA.
Key rulesAccurate, verifiable product information only. No health or medical claims unless allowed for the category. No other brands' names as keywords. Reference ("was") prices must be genuine.

TikTok Shop UK

WhatRule
Product titleAt least 15 characters. Maximum: check in the platform's help pages. Must be accurate and concise (product type, material, key features, quantity, size). No promotional wording (for example "x% off"), no shop URL or seller name, no mention of TikTok or other platforms, no symbols or special characters.
DescriptionAt least 30 words. Keep it concise and readable. Maximum: check in the platform's help pages. Claims must be genuine, accurate and verifiable.
ImagesUp to 9 square images, at least 800 x 800 pixels. Upload at least 3. No duplicates. No text or watermarks other than product branding. Colour images only. The main image shows the front of the product.
CommissionStandard platform commission of 9% (inclusive of VAT). Lower rates can apply to new sellers and some categories. Affiliate creator commission is extra and set by you.
Banned claimsNo medicines or medical devices. No claims that a product cures, treats, prevents or relieves any disease or condition, anywhere in the listing or video. No weight loss claims without diet and exercise, no before and after weight images, no claims that weight loss is easy, guaranteed or permanent.
AI contentRealistic AI-generated images or video must be labelled, and must not make the product look different from reality. Check the AIGC policy for detail.
Key rulesCheck the prohibited and restricted products lists before listing. Some categories need extra approval or documents. Keep orders and payment in TikTok Shop. Any discount must be real.

Beyond the platforms: UK rules worth knowing

These are not platform rules, and we have not verified the detail here. Please read the official pages yourself.

  • Selling as a business? Consumer rights on returns and faulty goods apply to traders. Read GOV.UK's guidance on accepting returns and giving refunds: https://www.gov.uk/accepting-returns-and-giving-refunds
  • Platform reporting to HMRC. Online platforms report some sellers' details to HMRC. Being reported does not by itself mean tax is due. Read: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/reporting-rules-for-digital-platforms
  • Trading allowance and tax. Read HMRC's guidance on tax-free allowances on trading income: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tax-free-allowances-on-property-and-trading-income

Last checked: September 2026. Rules change: always check the current rule in the platform's help pages before you list.
